items.abstract: Multimodal coding agents decouple 4D world construction from visual generation, repurposing video models from world generators toward generative renderers. This division of labor raises a fundamental question: if code builds the world, can video models just render it? A reliable generative renderer hinges on two complementary criteria: (i) world preservation, retaining prescribed 4D kinematics and camera paths; and (ii) visual realization, persistently binding text-specified target attributes over time. To evaluate this capability, we introduce WorldDraft, a benchmark of 432 strictly paired test cases across 48 executable 4D world families spanning six dynamic challenge categories. Under a 3 times 3 factorial design, WorldDraft orthogonally crosses draft granularity (abstract proxy to previs) and appearance alignment (neutral to conflicting) under identical dynamics. Extensive evaluations across 12 representative models reveal that: (I) world preservation and visual realization remain in stark operational tension; (II) richer draft scaffolding anchors structure but paradoxically impairs appearance fidelity; and (III) conflicting source cues trigger severe source leakage (up to 64%), exposing fragile cross-modal disentanglement. To mitigate these bottlenecks, we propose WorldDraft-Primer, a plug-and-play visual prompting strategy that consistently improves both objectives across frozen video renderers. Together, WorldDraft and WorldDraft-Primer lay a foundation for bridging programmatic 4D simulation with video generation, advancing physically grounded generative rendering.

items.abstract: We present UniSpark-9B, a unified multimodal model that investigates hybrid attention for visual understanding and generation. Built on a Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts backbone with approximately 9B parameters in each branch, UniSpark combines full attention for explicit token interactions with GatedDeltaNet linear attention for compact context propagation. Autoregressive text prediction and visual flow matching jointly support visual question answering, text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and interleaved text-image prediction. In interleaved generation, noisy visual targets are isolated from subsequent predictions, while clean visual representations provide context for later outputs. A blockwise protocol enforces this distinction through attention masks in full-attention layers and recurrent-state retention rules in linear-attention layers. The selected training sources contain 159.7M generation samples, 213.4M understanding samples, and 624.8K interleaved sequences. A four-stage curriculum jointly trains multimodal understanding and visual generation, refining answer accuracy and instruction following while extending image synthesis to 2K. UniSpark scores 2470.3 on MME-S and 0.83 on GenEval. Qualitative examples further illustrate its capabilities in interleaved image generation, video synthesis, and video editing. Together, these results demonstrate that hybrid attention provides an effective backbone for unified multimodal understanding and generation.

items.abstract: Video generation models produce visually realistic videos but still struggle with physical dynamics and causal consistency. Learning from generated videos requires fine-grained physical supervision, yet reliable quality judgments, correction pairs, and controlled variations are difficult to obtain. Large language models (LLMs) possess physical knowledge, but struggle to reliably guide video generation models in producing their training videos. We present PhysLoop, a unified harness designed to support physically grounded self-improvement in video generation models. The harness guides and constrains LLMs throughout video generation, selection, and correction, distilling their physical knowledge into physically consistent videos. The framework supports controllable training-data construction and inference-time video repair. By identifying and correcting failures, PhysLoop marks a key milestone toward recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video generation models with limited human intervention. We release 100K videos spanning diverse, realistic indoor and outdoor scenes, along with generation tools and two evaluation datasets: PhysLoop-Gen and PhysLoop-Repair. We evaluate controllable generation and localized repair on these datasets, respectively, and assess physical behavior on the external Physics-IQ Verified benchmark.

items.abstract: Transferring LLMs into System One decision models typically replaces the language modeling head with a decision head while retaining the full backbone, making every decision pay for all layers. Yet it remains unclear how much depth such decisions require. We find that decision information is concentrated in intermediate layers, with early layers building essential features and the final six layers removable without loss, while independently trained smaller models largely mimic the full model rather than developing specialized decision capabilities. These findings suggest that efficiency requires not simply smaller backbones, but shared computation across different depths. Building on this, we propose , which jointly trains a full model with prefix sub-models that share its final layers and decision head through self-distillation. A lightweight gate reads the hidden state at each exit to determine whether additional computation is needed, allowing one model to operate at multiple layers. Across seven decision benchmarks, our approach matches or outperforms independently trained models at every depth, while achieving better accuracy-efficiency trade-offs through adaptive computation.

items.title: Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Internal Validation Reveal the Mechanism by Which β-Ecdysterone Combined with Paeoniflorin Alleviates Oxidative Stress-Induced Damage in Parkinson’s Disease via the Nrf2 Pathway

items.abstract: Abstract Background Oxidative stress induces dopaminergic apoptosis and accelerates Parkinson’s disease (PD). The Nrf2 pathway mediates central antioxidant defense. β-ecdysone (β-Ecd) and paeoniflorin (PF) produce Nrf2-dependent neuroprotection alone, while their combined anti-PD mechanism remains unknown. This study used bioinformatics, machine learning, molecular docking, 100-ns MD simulations and MPTP-PD mice to explore their synergy and Nrf2-mediated neuroprotection. Methods TCMSP screened herbal ingredients. Drug-PD targets and PD DEGs were retrieved from databases and GEO. Overlapping targets underwent GO/KEGG enrichment; core targets filtered by LASSO, Random Forest and SVM-RFE were validated by independent GEO data.Molecular docking and 100 ns MD simulations assessed ligand-receptor binding. PD mice were divided into control, model, selegiline, β-Ecd, PF and combination groups. Motor function, nigral neuronal morphology, antioxidant indices and the expression of DA markers, total HSP90AA1, total and phosphorylated PRKCB and STAT3, Nrf2 downstream HO-1/NQO1 and apoptosis-related proteins were detected. Results Twenty-two drug-disease intersecting targets were obtained. Enrichment analysis highlighted oxidative stress closely associated with Nrf2 signaling. STAT3, HSP90AA1 and PRKCB were identified as core targets. Molecular simulations verified favorable binding affinity between the two compounds and the three proteins. In PD mice, combined β-Ecd and PF reversed molecular abnormalities, activated Nrf2-dependent HO-1/NQO1, restored antioxidant capacity and suppressed neuronal apoptosis. Its neuroprotective effect was superior to single-drug treatment and comparable to selegiline. Conclusions β-Ecd combined with PF protects dopaminergic neurons by targeting HSP90AA1-PRKCB-STAT3 and indirectly activating Nrf2 antioxidant signaling in PD mice.

items.abstract: Treponema pallidum subsp. pallidum ( TPA) , an obligate bacterial pathogen that causes the sexually transmitted disease syphilis, is an extreme auxotroph with a minimal genome and distinct parasitic lifestyle. Approximately 17% of its 977 annotated proteins lack a predicted function because they show little sequence similarity to proteins of known function from other organisms. We therefore utilized the robust structural modeling and matching capabilities of AlphaFold and FoldSeek to create a whole-proteome atlas for the Nichols type strain of this bacterium ( TPANIC ), with the goal of providing structure-based functional assignments for uncharacterized proteins and verifying the accuracy of annotations previously generated by protein sequence homology analysis alone. Using a combination of precomputed structures from the AlphaFold Database and newly generated AlphaFold 3 structural predictions, we produced high-confidence predicted structural models for approximately 92% of the TPANIC proteome, enabling us to identify structural homologs and assign potential functional annotations to 24 previously uncharacterized proteins. Beyond functional annotation, the updated genome-derived structural models revealed several major structural revisions resulting from corrected gene models. Most notably, integration of comparative structural analyses and AlphaFold-Multimer modeling redefined the composition of the TPA outer membrane biogenesis machinery, supporting the existence of a conserved spirochete-specific BAM-TAM complex containing BamA, TamB, BamD, and BamB. We anticipate that the resulting AlphaFold protein structure atlas, in combination with the recently developed tools of in vitro cultivation and genetic manipulation, will help elucidate the roles of TPANIC proteins in the organism's biology, pathogenesis, and host immune interactions.IMPORTANCEIncidence of syphilis has been on the rise in the past decade, emphasizing the need to understand the mechanisms behind the persistence and virulence of its causative agent, Treponema pallidum . In this study, we employed a next-generation artificial intelligence-based protein structure modeling and matching pipeline, building upon prior structural conservation studies by expanding the functional predictions for hypothetical proteins. Consequently, this study provides a clearer picture of the metabolic and pathogenic capabilities of this elusive pathogen, while highlighting the intricacies of its regulatory landscape. We anticipate that our strategy will complement existing sequence-homology-based gene/genome annotation pipelines, assisting in both protein function validation and the identification of orthologous proteins lacking sequence homology.

items.abstract: Co-folding models are increasingly used to predict antibody-antigen complexes for epitope mapping, candidate triage and structure-guided de novo design or engineering, yet the latest generation of these models has not been compared under standardized conditions. We benchmark AlphaFold 3, Protenix-v2, ESMFold2, ESMFold2-fast and OpenDDE on 200 test-set complexes (121 Fvs and 79 V H Hs) from SAbDab2-Bench, a newly curated dataset, and a reconstructed antibody-antigen subset of FoldBench, Ab-FoldBench. Using standardized inputs, sampling, and interface metrics that isolate the antibody-antigen interface, we compare docking accuracy, inference-time scaling, confidence-based candidate structure selection and sensitivity to interaction perturbations. OpenDDE achieved the highest median DockQ and docking pass rate, followed by Protenix-v2, although their difference was not statistically significant. Both models outperformed AlphaFold 3 on these measures, alongside offering fewer licensing restrictions on model and prediction use. We further find that model confidence was generally effective at identifying accurate predictions but showed model-dependent variations. To probe interaction specificity, which is essential for antibody design, we generated decoys through non-conservative interface mutations, and non-cognate antigen shuffling. Confidence decreased for both perturbations, but more consistently for non-cognate antigens than for interface mutations, with OpenDDE retaining comparatively high confidence for many decoys. Overall, Protenix-v2 combined high docking accuracy with strong rejection of perturbed interfaces, OpenDDE achieved the highest docking accuracy, albeit at the longest runtime, while ESMFold2-fast offered the fastest inference for large-scale triage. These results provide an up-to-date guidance framework for selecting and configuring co-folding models in antibody discovery, design, and engineering.

items.abstract: Abstract Olimarabidopsis pumila ( O. pumila ) is an annual spring ephemeral mustard plant that possesses adaptations to its semi-arid and salinized desert environments, affording it high salinity tolerance and the ability to maintain efficient photosynthesis under high-intensity solar radiation [1]. Four genes were identified between base pairs 7,500,000 and 8,000,000 on contig tig00002140 using the Genomic Sequence Annotation Server (GenSAS) and AUGUSTUS [2, 3]. Sequence conservation was assessed using the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Protein Basic Local Alignment Search Tool (BLASTP) and Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) Viewer [4, 5]. Localization was determined using WoLF PSORT, SignalP 6.0, and Transmembrane Hidden Markov Models (TMHMM) 2.0 [6, 7, 8]. Lastly, structural analysis was configured using InterProScan, AlphaFold, STRING, and the combination of UniProt and ColabFold [9, 10, 11, 12, 13]. The four gene models were predicted to encode a DnaJ‑family chaperone that assists in protein folding, an indole‑3‑glycerol phosphate synthase used in tryptophan biosynthesis, a ribosomal RNA‑processing protein involved in rRNA maturation, and a protein with a GEF domain that is annotated as a ubiquitin ligase [9]. These four gene models are candidates for roles in protein translation, cellular homeostasis, signaling, and hormone biosynthesis that may contribute to plant growth and stress resilience.

items.abstract: Cancer remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, necessitating continuous advances in therapeutic strategies to improve treatment efficacy and patient outcomes. Over recent decades, cancer management has evolved from conventional cytotoxic approaches toward more sophisticated, individualized interventions that target specific molecular alterations and harness the immune system. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the paradigm shift in cancer treatment, tracing the evolution from conventional chemotherapy to modern precision oncology and immunotherapy. We examine traditional diagnostic staging and highlight the integration of liquid biopsies and advanced biosensor technologies for real-time, non-invasive clinical monitoring. The review explores the mechanistic pillars of cell cycle-specific and non-specific chemotherapeutic agents, alongside the complex multidrug resistance pathways and metabolic rewiring that drive chemoresistance. We also evaluate the growing efficacy of targeted treatments, including small-molecule kinase inhibitors and antibody-drug conjugates, and detail the transformative clinical impact of immune checkpoint inhibitors, CAR-T cell therapies, and therapeutic vaccines. Emphasizing personalized medicine, we discuss the critical role of pharmacogenomics, biomarker-guided therapies, and the integration of artificial intelligence and quantitative systems pharmacology in optimizing dosing. Finally, we address future directions, including CRISPR-engineered cellular therapies and the modulation of the hypoxic tumor microenvironment using natural phytochemicals.

items.abstract: CATH (https://www.cathdb.info) is a widely used bioinformatics resource that classifies protein structural domains from the wwPDB and integrates evolutionary, structural, and functional annotation alongside interactive visualization and analysis tools. CATH is recognized as a Core Data Resource by ELIXIR and a Global Core Biodata Resource by the Global Biodata Coalition. CATH continues to expand its coverage of protein structure space by integrating experimentally determined structures from the Protein Data Bank with the rapidly growing collections of predicted structures from the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database as part of The Encyclopedia of Domains, the new sister resource of CATH. We provide an update on advances in new homology detection protocols and automated workflows providing end-to-end domain annotation and classification for processing large-scale protein structural data.

items.abstract: Background: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) myocarditis affects up to 2% of patients on ICI and has up to a 50% mortality. Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) is a risk factor for ICI myocarditis. Objectives: To leverage a multi-omics approach to evaluate cytokines associated with ICI myocarditis, immunosuppression resistance, CHIP in ICI myocarditis and implicated pathways and cell type contributions. Methods 236 cardio-oncology patients were enrolled, including 88 who were on ICI. Cytokine profiling from patients on ICI were sampled and analyzed using machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence. Single-cell multi-omics of peripheral blood from Yale (n=19), Stanford (n=25), and MGH (n=63) evaluated cell-type contributions of cytokines and implicated pathways. Validation of Yale proteomic analyses was done using the Stanford CYTOF dataset. Results Top features associated with ICI myocarditis included IL13, CXCL10, PDGFA, CCL13, CCL17 and KITlg. Top KEGG pathways associated with ICI myocarditis and immunosuppression resistant ICI myocarditis included JAK STAT signaling, IL17 signaling and lipid/atherosclerosis pathways. At the single-cell level, the consensus signals distinguishing myocarditis from non-myocarditis across cohorts was predominantly driven by module-level JAK STAT, T cell, and Toll like receptor activation. Similar transcription gene programs were activated in CHIP carriers including modules implicated in the pro-inflammatory immune response, such as NF kappa B, IL17, MAPK, and TNF pathways within CHIP cells spanning lymphoid (cytotoxic CD8+ NKT, and natural killer cells) and myeloid lineages. Conclusions Across cohorts, JAK STAT signaling emerges as a convergent and potentially actionable axis in ICI myocarditis that is further amplified in CHIP carriers, supporting cytokine-guided risk stratification and JAK STAT directed immunosuppression as testable strategies.

items.abstract: The central nervous system (CNS) comprises diverse cell types whose molecular context shapes the roles of the proteins they express. Computational models offer a scalable way to study the roles of proteins across human brain cell types, with protein language models and interactome- or single-cell-based models capturing complementary information encoded in protein sequences and cellular network contexts. Human brain tissue is hard to access, so brain cell types make up a small fraction of the atlases single-cell models train on and of the benchmarks used for their evaluation. To capture these complementary sources of information in the CNS, we introduce SEMPER, a multimodal representation learning model that aligns protein language model representations with protein-protein interaction networks from 442 cell types of the adult human brain, giving each protein a sequence-informed representation in every cell type in which its gene is expressed. We show that SEMPER representations predict cell type-specific protein complexes and predict genes essential to the survival of dopaminergic neurons, measured in a genome-wide CRISPR screen. In zero-shot retrieval, SEMPER recovers clinically pursued drug targets for Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, Huntington's disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis at higher rates than cell type-specific models. To further improve target recovery, we combine SEMPER with a large language model that reasons over protein functional annotations. The combination recovers more targets, with SEMPER providing experimentally derived cellular context that complements literature-based reasoning of the large language model.

items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning are being applied rapidly across autoimmune neurological disorders, but the overall shape of this literature — which disorders, data modalities and methods dominate, and where evidence is absent — has not been quantified. Objective. To map the published research landscape of AI in autoimmune neurological disorders through a bibliometric analysis, and to identify the field’s concentrations and gaps. Methods. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched in November 2026 using a title/abstract strategy combining terms for autoimmune neurological disorders (multiple sclerosis [MS], NMOSD, MOGAD, autoimmune encephalitis, autoimmune epilepsy, paraneoplastic neurological syndromes) with artificial-intelligence and machine-learning terms, limited to 2015–2026. Records were analysed programmatically for annual output, leading journals, authorship, open-access status, and disorder-, modality- and method-level focus (title-level tagging). Results. 1,455 records were analysed. Annual output rose from 10 (2015) to 270 (2025), with 2026 already at 319 ahead-of-print records; output grew approximately 12-fold between 2015–2018 and 2022– 2025. The literature was dominated by multiple sclerosis (883 records, 60.7%), with all other disorders comparatively rare (NMOSD 45; autoimmune encephalitis 26; MOGAD 11; paraneoplastic 1). MRI was the dominant data modality (517 records, 35.5%), whereas EEG (9), genomics (25) and CSF biomarkers (83) were seldom addressed. Only 33 records (2.3%) described multimodal or data-fusion approaches. Deep learning (259) had overtaken classical machine learning (226). Work was distributed across 463 journals (led by Multiple Sclerosis and Related Disorders, n=84); 63.9% of records were open access. Conclusions. Research on AI in autoimmune neurology is expanding steeply but is heavily concentrated on multiple sclerosis and MRI. Rarer disorders, electrophysiological, fluid-biomarker and genomic data, and genuine multimodal integration remain markedly under-explored — defining clear priorities for future work.

items.abstract: Motivation The rapid advancement of spatial transcriptomics (ST) has established a foundation for the complementary integration of multimodal information from gene expression profiles, spatial localization, and histological images. However, noise and data heterogeneity complicate the characterization of spatial relationships and tissue structure. Results In this study, we develop a deep learning framework, CroSP, based on a multi-view graph autoencoder. The framework integrates gene expression profiles, spatial locations, and tissue morphology information into a low-dimensional latent representation. Cross-view contrastive learning and metric learning coordinate the complementary views. Across datasets from multiple platforms and spatial resolutions, CroSP improved spatial domain identification and delineated brain and olfactory bulb structures. Analyses using established downstream methods further characterized spatially variable genes and the spatial heterogeneity, immune microenvironments, and cell-cell communication in human breast cancer tissue. These results support the use of CroSP for spatial biological analysis in healthy and diseased tissues. Availability and implementation Source code and tutorials: https://github.com/Biowust/CroSP.git. Archived code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22675113. items.abstract: Microfluidic impedance cytometry (MIC) is a critical technology for high-throughput single-cell analysis owing to its label-free, non-invasive operation and ease of integration. However, under high-throughput conditions, baseline drift, noise, and multi-cell coincidence events distort cell counting and amplitude estimation. To enhance detection accuracy, this work presents a single-cell signal detection system based on a coplanar three-electrode differential impedance microchip, in which deep learning is integrated with a sparse recovery algorithm. Raw impedance signals acquired by the three-electrode differential configuration are first processed by a recurrent neural network (RNN) to automatically identify and precisely segment cell events. Subsequently, a one dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) is introduced to classify the number of coincident particles in each event segment, and the classification results are used as the sparsity prior for the sparse recovery algorithm. Based on this prior, an -norm-based sparse recovery algorithm separates multi particle coincident waveforms and accurately recovers single-cell amplitudes. Validation experiments using human lymphoma cells verify that our system achieves precise particle event segmentation, reliable identification of coincident particle counts, and high-precision recovery of single-particle amplitude characteristics. Overall, the proposed detection framework effectively improves the accuracy and operability of MIC single-cell analysis in the presence of coincident particles, laying a scalable technical foundation for high-throughput and intelligent single-cell measurement in subsequent studies.

items.abstract: Objective To develop and validate an artificial intelligence (AI) model that can identify kidney stone composition more accurately than the EQUIL2 urine supersaturation (SS) algorithm. Patients and methods Patients with both a 24-hour urine SS panel and a kidney stone composition analysis conducted within 90 days of each other between September 24, 2015, and March 15, 2024, were identified (n=13,000 unique patients). Kidney stones were classified as either majority calcium oxalate (CaOx), majority calcium phosphate (CaP), uric acid, or other. A model was developed to predict kidney stone classification using demographic characteristics plus urinary SS panel results. This model was subsequently validated on a held-out data set of paired measurements collected between March 16, 2024, and March 15, 2025 (n=1653). The urinary SS for CaOx, hydroxyapatite (CaP), brushite (CaP), and uric acid were calculated using EQUIL2 according to routine clinical practice and expressed using the delta Gibbs free energy scale. Results The AI model was significantly more accurate in the validation data set for identifying stone composition compared with SS alone (accuracy, 0.73 vs 0.33; P<.01). Additionally, the model outperformed SS alone in the validation data set for correctly identifying kidney stone composition in all analyses stratified into clinically relevant subgroups by age and sex. Conclusion In all kidney stone categories and within various subgroups, the AI model outperformed the EQUIL2-calculated SS as well as previously published AI models in the correct prediction of CaOx, CaP, and uric acid kidney stones when using the 24-hour urine SS panel.

items.abstract: Traditional models of medical education are increasingly challenged by structural and logistical constraints. In Dermato-Venereology, there is marked heterogeneity in undergraduate training across Europe, including substantial variation in curriculum structure and the perceived importance of the speciality. The aim of this study was to develop harmonized, structured and scalable educational tools for blended learning within an interactive "flipped classroom" framework. Within an EU-funded Erasmus+ project, supported by the European Dermatology Forum, key structural gaps in current training were identified, and a conceptual framework for restructuring undergraduate Dermato-Venereology education was developed. This framework emphasizes harmonization and standardization, scalability and integration into clinical practice. The development process incorporated iterative feedback from participating centres and alignment with existing European educational standards. The e-learning platform Cyberderm was expanded, revised and harmonized, and complemented by a more detailed PDF-based version ("webbook"), accessible electronically, to provide standardized educational content across European training settings. In addition, an artificial intelligence-based feature was implemented, enabling query-driven navigation and facilitating intuitive access to content. This functionality supports individualized learning pathways and enhances adaptability to different levels of training and educational needs. These results provide the first set of recommendations for a harmonized European undergraduate training programme in Dermato-Venereology.

items.abstract: Background and objectives Craniopagus twins (CPT) represent one of the rarest forms of conjoined twinning, and their surgical separation demands meticulous preoperative planning. We describe the evolution of an integrated surgical planning pipeline combining patient-specific 3-dimensional (3D) printed models, tissue-mimicking materials (TMM), and immersive virtual reality (VR) across 3 consecutive CPT cases at a single institution, and discuss the emerging role of artificial intelligence-driven segmentation as the next translational step. Methods Three CPT cases were managed at the Ribeirão Preto Medical School (University of São Paulo, Brazil). Cases 1 and 2 were completed separations using an incremental prototyping pipeline: computed tomography/MRI-based segmentation, virtual modeling, fused deposition modeling 3D printing with polylactic acid, and silicone rubber or latex covering as TMM. Case 3 continued immersive VR visualization using a Meta Quest 3 headset, enabling the multidisciplinary team to rehearse surgical steps in a simulated operating room. Results Thirteen patient-specific models were produced across the 3 cases over approximately 36 months. The pipeline matured progressively: Case 1 established the core workflow; case 2 refined TMM application and skin-surface calculations; cases 2 and 3 integrated VR-based immersive briefings. Separation was achieved in all 3 pairs; in case 3, however, both twins died intraoperatively from hemorrhage and cardiogenic shock with refractory circulatory collapse, despite anatomically accurate planning models. Team feedback indicated that VR enhanced spatial understanding of the shared vascular anatomy and improved preoperative coordination vs flat-screen visualization. Conclusion The progressive integration of VR into an established 3D printing pipeline represents a meaningful advance in CPT separation planning. Artificial intelligence-driven segmentation tools hold promise for automating the bottleneck step, potentially making this pipeline replicable across institutions with fewer specialized resources.

items.abstract: The rising global incidence of arrhythmia calls for reliable detection methods. Most existing approaches suffer from poor generalization and insufficient feature extraction for long-term electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. This work proposes an adaptive multi-scale dilated convolutional network (AMSDNet). It uses multi-scale dilated convolutions, gated adaptive weight allocation, and spatial attention fusion to capture global ECG features. Validated on Massachusetts Institute of Technology-Beth Israel Hospital Arrhythmia Database (MIT-BIH), the China Physiological Signal Challenge (CPSC) 2018, and the Computing in Cardiology Challenge (CINC) 2017 datasets, our method outperforms state-of-the-art models with average accuracy of 99.7%, 91.8% and 83.7%, respectively.

items.abstract: Background Predicting outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is challenging. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict outcomes after EVT using only clinical characteristics available shortly after hospital arrival, excluding imaging, laboratory, and angiographic data. Methods We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke. A total of 4353 patients who underwent EVT between 2016 and 2020 were included, with those from 2016 to 2019 assigned to the derivation cohort and those from 2020 to the validation cohort. The model was developed using 132 routinely collected clinical variables that can be rapidly obtained on patient arrival. Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm, and the model was built using CatBoost. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0 to 2 at discharge. Results Among 4353 patients treated with EVT, the derivation cohort included 2764 patients and the validation cohort, 1589 patients. In these cohorts, 973 (35.2%) and 547 (34.4%) achieved mRS 0 to 2, respectively. Boruta selected 47 predictors. CatBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.744 (95% CI, 0.710-0.776) in the derivation test set and 0.781 (95% CI, 0.755-0.803) in the validation cohort. Validation areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves were 0.792 (95% CI, 0.765-0.815) for mRS 0 to 1, 0.766 (95% CI, 0.744-0.787) for mRS 0 to 3, and 0.680 (95% CI, 0.631-0.729) for mRS 6. Conclusions Our machine learning model predicted outcomes following EVT using only admission clinical data. This imaging-independent machine learning approach may support early prognostication and facilitate discussions of expected clinical courses.

items.abstract: BackgroundAccurate classification and segmentation of brain tumors from medical images are essential for reliable diagnosis and treatment planning. However, variations in image quality, noise, and tumor characteristics can complicate automated analysis.ObjectiveThis study aims to develop a deep learning framework for the accurate classification and segmentation of brain tumors by integrating an ensemble convolutional neural network (CNN) with the Riesz-Quincunx WaVnet Chaotic Rime Attention Encoder.MethodsThe proposed framework incorporates image preprocessing techniques to enhance contrast, reduce noise, and improve image quality. The ensemble CNN is integrated with the Riesz-Quincunx WaVnet Chaotic Rime Attention Encoder to strengthen feature extraction and representation. The framework is designed to identify brain abnormalities and classify tumor subregions, including necrotic tumor cores, enhancing tumors, peritumoral edematous areas, and non-enhancing tumor cores. Furthermore, a Flask-based web application is developed to facilitate remote access and support clinical collaboration.ResultsThe proposed framework is designed to improve brain tumor classification and segmentation by combining ensemble learning with enhanced feature representation. However, quantitative performance metrics are required to substantiate its diagnostic accuracy, segmentation performance, and superiority over existing methods.ConclusionThe proposed deep learning framework integrates image preprocessing, ensemble CNN classification, and attention-based feature extraction to support automated brain tumor analysis. Its Flask-based deployment offers potential for remote accessibility and telemedicine applications, supporting medical specialists in diagnostic decision-making. Further validation using quantitative performance metrics and independent clinical datasets is necessary to establish its clinical reliability.

items.abstract: BackgroundBrain diseases pose a significant global health challenge, and their diagnosis often relies on subjective clinical assessments.ObjectiveTo this end, this study proposes an integrated wavelet signal processing and machine learning framework for single-channel Electroencephalography (EEG)-based detection of brain diseases with representative channel selection.MethodsFirst, EEG signals are decomposed into rhythm-specific sub-bands using the Discrete Wavelet Packet Transform (DWPT). Then, for each rhythm, a multi-dimensional feature matrix (MFM) is constructed by integrating Approximate Entropy (AE), Rhythm Energy Ratio (RER), C0-complexity (C0), and Zero-crossing Rate (ZCR), which comprehensively models the EEG characteristics. Six classifiers were compared under subject-level leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, and Decision Tree (DT) was selected as the representative classifier. Each channel was then evaluated independently as a complete single-channel system, and representative channels were identified from the completed results.ResultsValidated on publicly available datasets for SCHIZ (schizophrenia), UNM (Parkinson's disease), and MPHCE (depression), the method achieves impressive accuracies of 84.52% (F4), 86.54% (F4), and 93.10% (Fp1), respectively, using single-channel EEG electrode.ConclusionsSuch results demonstrate that the proposed approach maintains robust detection performance in each of the three disease-specific tasks. The framework is lightweight by design, using only a single EEG channel and a single simple machine-learning model for classification. It needs no multi-channel feature concatenation or decision-level fusion. This single-channel design suits hardware and data sources with limited resources, and may support the development of low-cost portable EEG systems.

items.abstract: Purpose To compare agreement between total corneal astigmatism (TCA) predictions from a deep learning (DL) model and those from the Barrett Toric Calculator (Barrett) and Abulafia-Koch (AK) formulas. Methods In 100 eyes with corneal astigmatism, Pentacam HR imaging (Oculus Optikgeräte GmbH) was used to generate TCA predictions with the AK formula, Barrett formula, and a previously validated DL model. Agreement was assessed using Pearson and Spearman correlation, mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and Bland-Altman analysis. Clinical interchangeability was predefined as 95% limits of agreement within ±0.25 diopters (D) for magnitude and ±5 degrees for axis. Predictions were also decomposed into Cartesian X and Y vector components. Results The AK and Barrett formulas demonstrated near-perfect agreement for both magnitude ( r = 0.99; MAE: 0.070 D, RMSE: 0.11 D) and axis ( r = 1.00; MAE: 1.11°, RMSE: 1.68°), with 95% limits of agreement both within the interchangeability thresholds. Compared with both conventional methods, the DL model showed larger systematic differences. Compared with the Barrett formula, magnitude agreement was r = 0.92 (MAE: 0.24 D; RMSE: 0.27 D), and axis agreement was r = 1.00 (MAE: 4.71 degrees). Similar findings were observed versus the AK formula (magnitude r = 0.94, MAE: 0.20 D; axis MAE: 4.92°). The DL model consistently underestimated X-components relative to both traditional methods (RMSE: 0.28 to 0.31 D), whereas Y-component agreement was excellent across all pairs (RMSE ⩽ 0.05 D). DL axis differences followed a sinusoidal pattern with astigmatism orientation ( R 2 = 0.84 to 0.87), peaking at oblique meridians. Conclusions The AK and Barrett formulas are clinically interchangeable for TCA prediction, with limits of agreement falling entirely within established toric intraocular lens planning thresholds. The DL model exhibits systematic, yet consistent deviations from both traditional methods that demonstrate lack of interchangeability. Prospective studies comparing postoperative refractive outcomes for each method are required to determine whether the DL model's deviations represent superior predictive performance.

items.abstract: Objective Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes are rapidly becoming normalized in clinical practice, yet governance frameworks focus on accuracy, privacy, consent, and medicolegal status. Risks to clinician capabilities have received less attention. Speak before the reveal is a proposed method in which clinicians verbalize critical cognitive steps, such as synthesis and plan, before note generation. Discussion Recent work distinguishes deskilling in senior clinicians, never-skilling from premature offload in trainees and mis-skilling, the internalization of AI errors and inappropriate use as sound practice. This Perspective builds on emerging evidence that reasoning before seeing AI output may protect unaided reasoning. Training implementation, evaluation, adherence challenges, validation methodology, and governance strategies for training bodies, health services, and scribe vendors are discussed. Conclusion Speak before the reveal is a low-cost, testable approach to maintaining clinical reasoning for individuals or organizations. Successful AI scribe adoption requires preserving clinicians' ability to work without AI support.

items.abstract: Postmarketing pharmacovigilance relies on spontaneous adverse event reporting and labor-intensive observational studies, which suffer from underreporting and delayed risk detection. Large language model (LLM) agents could automate real-world evidence generation, but generalist agents make ad hoc analytical decisions that compromise epidemiological validity and reproducibility. Here we present MedCheckpoint, a multi-agent LLM system for automated postmarketing pharmacovigilance. MedCheckpoint grounds each analytical stage in a curated, source-traceable medical knowledge base, locks core study-design parameters before execution, performs patient-level analyses with human-written deterministic statistical tools, and enforces checkpoint rules that abort infeasible analyses, with optional human-in-the-loop review. We evaluated MedCheckpoint using a 54-question benchmark on a dual-purpose simulated electronic health record (EHR) testbed of 2.7 million individuals, designed with reliable clinical signals to evaluate routine analytical accuracy alongside spurious signals to stress-test system rigor. Across the benchmark, MedCheckpoint outperformed two coding-agent baselines in report quality across five dimensions rated by three independent LLM judges (overall means 4.81-4.88 versus 4.25-4.55 and 4.02-4.29) and yielded higher run-to-run consistency (mean within-question standard deviation 0.116-0.186 versus up to 0.440). Crucially, while baselines failed on up to 2 of 21 runs when handling infeasible comparisons or unmeasurable outcomes, MedCheckpoint produced no misleading failures across all seven stress-test trap questions with known data limitations. MedCheckpoint enables reliable, auditable, and scalable pharmacovigilance analysis.

items.abstract: Background: FDA-cleared artificial intelligence (AI) triage tool for pulmonary embolism (PE) detection has been widely used; however, its performance has not been analyzed for subgroups, clinical sites, and temporal stability. Methods. This retrospective, six-site health system study evaluated the Aidoc BriefCase PE triage model (K190072) across 14,736 CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) examinations between July 2023 and March 2026. Reference-standard PE characteristic labels were extracted from radiology reports using a zero-shot LLM pipeline validated against a radiologist-annotated 600 reports (κ =0.98). Model performance was evaluated across demographics, embolus characteristics, and site. Temporal behavior was evaluated on operating point by logistic regression, with and without site adjustment, and by segmented regression. Results. PE was present in 1,402/14,736 examinations (9.5%). Overall sensitivity was 64.1% (95% CI, 61.5-66.6%), specificity 98.8% (95% CI, 98.6-99.0%), compared with 93% sensitivity and 93.7% specificity in the FDA 510(k) summary. Sensitivity fell with peripherality (central 88.6%, lobar or segmental 63.1%, subsegmental 33.3%) and with chronicity (acute 65.5%, chronic 57.4%). Sensitivity differed significantly between the two highest-volume sites, 68.7% and 55.7% (P < .001), with CT scanner as the only variable different between the two sites. The false-positive rate fell 40% per year (P<.001) at a similar rate at two sites, while sensitivity fell 15% per year at site A (P<.036), from 72.5% to 65.0% between two halves of the study period. The manufacturer did not report model updates or threshold changes during the study period. Conclusions. Deployed sensitivity was substantially below the cleared benchmark and varied 13 points by site. The gradual shift in high specificity at the cost of low sensitivity, either from data drift or threshold change, either not monitored or not documented by the manufacturer, highlights the importance of independent continuous post-market monitoring.

items.abstract: Background: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) may provide personalised and dynamically adjustable support for chronic disease self-management. However, previous studies have largely focused on isolated questions and a limited range of evaluation dimensions. Objective To compare the quality of self-management advice generated by GenAI and primary care physicians (PCPs) across multiple stages of chronic disease management and evaluation dimensions. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional, source-blinded comparative evaluation using 15 standardised vignettes of diabetes and hypertension derived from authentic primary care follow-up records. Each vignette comprised three sequential management stages, with medical accuracy, readability, and behaviour-change potential assessed across the three simulated stages; individualisation and multidisciplinary integration at plan initiation; contextual adaptability during acute adjustment; and empathy during long-term maintenance. The GenAI system and 22 PCPs independently generated advice which was independently rated by three clinicians，one each from general practice, endocrinology, and cardiology. across seven dimensions. Linear mixed-effects models were used for the primary comparisons, and case-level paired and physician-distribution analyses were conducted as robustness analyses. Results The GenAI system achieved estimated marginal means above 4.0 in all dimensions except readability. It scored significantly higher than PCPs in six of the seven dimensions, with adjusted mean differences ranging from 1.16 to 1.56 points (P<.001). Readability was the only exception, with no significant difference between GenAI and PCPs (−0.22, 95% CI −0.54 to 0.11; P=.19). The GenAI mean exceeded the individual means of all recruited PCPs in the six dimensions but ranked at approximately the 23rd percentile for readability. Conclusions Our findings indicated the GenAI system may generate more highly rated self-management advice than PCPs across most evaluated dimensions but offered no advantage in readability. These findings provide pre-implementation evidence for GenAI as a potential source of structured and adaptive chronic disease self-management support. Patient-level pilot studies and subsequent randomised trials are needed to determine its acceptability and effects on behaviour and clinical outcomes.

items.abstract: Background: Loss-of-function mutations in MBD4 (methyl-CpG-binding domain protein 4) cause a specialized base excision repair (BER) deficiency characterized by hypermutated CpG>TpG signatures and sensitivity to immune checkpoint blockade. However, post-immunotherapy treatment prioritization remains empirically unmapped. In clinical oncology, DNA damage response (DDR) defects are frequently extrapolated to poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARPi) sensitivity by analogy to homologous recombination deficiency (HRD), without testing whether upstream glycosylase loss generates the nicked single-strand break (SSB) intermediates required for toxic PARP1-DNA trapping. Methods: We developed a three-axis framework integrating mechanistic curation, large-scale pharmacogenomics (DepMap 24Q2 CRISPR/RNA-seq, n=1,517; GDSC2 dose-response profiling, n=928; PRISM Repurposing), and a 5-Layer De-confounded Synthetic Lethality Machine Learning (SL-ML) Engine (SL-XGBRanker). To prevent functional dilution from variants of uncertain significance, MBD4 loss-of-function (MBD4-LOF) was strictly restricted to truncating and canonical splice-site alleles (21 of 36 mutated lines), independently validated by nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD; two-sided p2s = 0.0367), while excluding 15 lines harboring 19 non-truncating variants (18 missense, 1 inframe deletion). All primary pharmacogenomic comparisons were evaluated using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests (p2s), bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs), Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (BH-FDR) multiplicity correction across six pre-specified candidate axes, and Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) for expression equivalence. Results: Our analysis delineates three distinct therapeutic axes in MBD4-LOF tumors: (1) Cytidine Analog Vulnerability (Axis 1): Mechanistic structural evidence demonstrates that MBD4 loss impairs excision of 5-substituted pyrimidine analogs and deaminated bases, creating a direct biochemical bottleneck to gemcitabine and 5-fluorouracil incorporation. (2) ATR-Check1 Replication-Stress Vulnerability (Axis 2): In GDSC2 profiling, MBD4-LOF cell lines exhibit significant sensitivity to the ATR inhibitor ceralasertib (AZD6738). In the clinically relevant TP53-mutant background-which disables the G1/S checkpoint and forces reliance on ATR-mediated S/G2 arrest-MBD4-LOF lines (n=11 vs n=619 WT) demonstrate pronounced ceralasertib hypersensitivity (Delta LN_IC50 = -1.07, 95% CI [-1.62, -0.41], Cohen's d = -0.74, p2s = 0.0060, BH-FDR q = 0.036; Delta AUC = -0.087, d = -0.89, p2s = 0.0017), with 11/11 leave-one-out (LOO) jackknife iterations retaining two-sided significance (p2s <= 0.014). This genotype-associated dependency remains robust in the unstratified pan-cancer cohort (n=14 vs n=914 WT; Delta LN_IC50 = -0.73, 95% CI [-1.31, -0.11], d = -0.50, p2s = 0.0430; Delta AUC = -0.056, d = -0.56, p2s = 0.0259) and after purging microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) lines (n=10 vs n=906 WT MSS; Delta LN_IC50 = -0.91, 95% CI [-1.50, -0.22], d = -0.62, p2s = 0.0307). By contrast, Wee1 inhibition (adavosertib; n=15 vs n=920 WT; Delta LN_IC50 = -0.35, p2s = 0.1667) does not reach statistical significance. (3) Absence of Single-Agent PARPi Sensitivity (Axis 3): While PARP1 transcript abundance strongly governs pan-cancer PARPi cytotoxicity across n=481 cell lines (rho = -0.416, p < 10^-21 across five clinical PARPi), MBD4-LOF tumors (n=19 vs n=1,498 WT) show zero compensatory PARP1 upregulation (median 6.77 vs 6.66 log2[TPM+1], Delta median = +0.11, 95% CI [-0.39, +0.71], p2s = 0.605; TOST equivalence p_TOST = 0.0199 within +/- 0.50 log2[TPM+1]). Direct GDSC2 evaluation of MBD4-LOF (n=8) versus WT (n=478) confirms complete absence of single-agent PARPi sensitization across talazoparib (p2s = 0.973), olaparib (p2s = 0.522), niraparib (p2s = 0.877), rucaparib (p2s = 0.804), veliparib (p2s = 0.538), and the composite 5-drug mean PARPi Z-score (Delta median Z = -0.024, 95% CI [-0.84, +0.60], p2s = 0.841). Under Leave-One-Anchor-Out cross-validation across 12 canonical DDR genes (370 gene-drug pairs), our 5-Layer De-confounded SL-ML Engine achieves an out-of-fold AUROC of 0.9716, AUPRC of 0.8007, and Top-1 accuracy of 82.86%, zero-shot ranking gemcitabine (#1) and ceralasertib (#2) as the top therapeutic dependencies for held-out MBD4 while rejecting all PARP inhibitors (ranks #13, #27, #28, #31). Conclusion: MBD4-LOF tumors exhibit a selective, TP53-potentiated pharmacological dependency on ATR kinase inhibition alongside mechanistic vulnerability to cytidine analogs, but lack both the nicked BER repair intermediates and the PARP1 target expression required for single-agent PARP inhibitor efficacy.

items.abstract: Multiple epidemiological studies have established obesity as an adverse factor in breast cancer incidence, progression, and clinical outcomes. However, the biological mechanisms underlying these associations remain incompletely understood. In peritumoral adipose tissue, obesity is associated with chronic inflammation, macrophage recruitment, and broader alterations in the local microenvironment. Whether these obesity-associated changes are accompanied by distinct morphologic features within the tumor and non-adipose stromal compartments remains unclear. In this study, we investigated whether an AI-based pathology foundation model could support the development of machine learning algorithms capable of identifying obesity-associated morphologic patterns in histopathology images, with a particular focus on tumor and stromal regions. In a cohort of 195 patients with breast cancer, machine learning models using vector embeddings from non-adipose stromal regions classified high BMI (≥30 kg/m 2 ) versus low BMI (<25 kg/m 2 ) with an average AUC of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.73-0.83), consistently outperforming models based on tumor-only or combined tumor-stroma regions. These obesity-associated stromal signatures were observed across subgroups defined by hormone-receptor status and age, indicating that they are not restricted to specific clinical populations. Complementary embedding-based dissimilarity analysis further showed that higher BMI was associated with reduced inter-patient heterogeneity in both tumor and stromal tissues. Overall, these findings suggest that obesity is associated with distinct morphologic alterations in both tumor and non-adipose stromal tissues. Notably, the stromal compartment emerged as a particularly informative indicator of obesity-associated morphology and demonstrated reduced inter-patient heterogeneity among individuals with high BMI.

items.abstract: Despite advances in targeted therapy, acquired resistance to osimertinib remains a major challenge in epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), owing to its biological heterogeneity, temporal evolution, and increasing therapeutic complexity. This narrative review critically examines the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to integrate clinical, molecular, imaging, and pharmacological data across the osimertinib treatment trajectory, with particular emphasis on resistance monitoring and clinical pharmacology. We discuss natural language processing for clinical data extraction and pharmacovigilance; digital pathology, radiomics, and multimodal learning for molecular pre-screening and risk stratification; longitudinal circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) modelling; and emerging applications of synthetic data, generative simulation, and digital twins. We also explore opportunities to integrate machine learning with pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modelling, exposure–response analyses, therapeutic drug monitoring, and model-informed precision dosing. Although selected AI approaches have demonstrated promising performance in retrospective studies and external or prospective silent evaluations, their ability to identify specific acquired resistance mechanisms and improve clinical outcomes through model-guided interventions remains unproven. Experience from other solid tumours provides methodological precedents, but disease-specific validation is required. Future progress will depend on multicentre longitudinal datasets integrating drug exposure, molecular evolution, treatment-related toxicity, and clinical outcomes, together with rigorous prospective evaluation. AI may complement established pharmacometric approaches to support more individualized, biologically informed treatment strategies in EGFR-mutated NSCLC.

items.abstract: Abstract Diagnosing gastric cancer still depends, for the most part, on a pathologist looking at stained tissue slides under a microscope. The disease kills roughly 660{,}000 people every year, and although early detection makes a real difference to survival, manual slide reading is slow and two experts examining the same slide do not always agree. In this work we built a system that tries to ease that burden. We trained a hybrid deep learning model on the Gastric Cancer Histopathology Tissue Image Dataset (GCHTID), pairing a Swin Transformer, which is good at picking up the broad structural layout of a tissue patch, with a ConvNeXt network, which captures the fine local textures where early malignant changes tend to hide. Every image first passes through a simple preprocessing chain of median filtering and CLAHE contrast enhancement, a combination we settled on after comparing several denoising and enhancement options. The ensemble sorts each patch into one of eight classes: tumor tissue (TUM) plus seven benign types-adipose, debris, lymphocytes, mucus, smooth muscle, normal mucosa, and stroma. On held-out data it reached 75.35% test accuracy (88.76% training, 76.99% best validation), beating the single-model baselines we tried, including ViT and EfficientNet-B3. To make the model usable outside a notebook, we wrapped it in a Flask REST API and a small web interface where a user can upload a slide image, see the prediction and its confidence, download a PDF report, and look back through past results. items.abstract: Abstract Background Computed tomography (CT) education benefits from prior examinations containing related localized findings. Whole-volume retrieval can be driven by global anatomy or unrelated findings, while database-specific retrieval models limit reuse. This study evaluates whether patch tokens from a frozen volumetric CT foundation encoder can support a reusable lesion-grounded retrieval framework without task-specific retrieval fine-tuning. Methods Spatial patch tokens were pooled into lesion representations linked to their parent examination, annotation, and source finding text. ReXGroundingCT served as the demonstration benchmark. The primary evaluation used FlexiCT-3D to search 14,359 reference lesions with 407 public-validation queries from 50 CT examinations. Exact masks, bounding boxes, and loose boxes tested sensitivity to query-region precision. Retrieval was evaluated against ontology-based relevance, analytic chance expectations, and annotation-informed descriptor controls. Results For exact-mask queries, exact-subcategory Recall@1 was 0.484, more than three times the analytic chance expectation of 0.154, while Recall@10 was 0.848 versus 0.729. Bounding-box and loose-box queries gave Recall@10 of 0.840 and 0.821, respectively, but less precise query regions lowered early-rank performance. Under both box policies, embedding retrieval outperformed the descriptor-only control. Conclusions A reusable lesion-retrieval layer can be built from frozen volumetric foundation features without task-specific retrieval training. The layer retains links to source finding text without using text for ranking and can organize compatible medical-image databases into lesion-centered ranked lists and localized review panels for educational case comparison.

items.abstract: Objectives To estimate standalone artificial intelligence (AI) diagnostic performance in temporomandibular joint (TMJ) imaging across input modality-target pairings. Methods Four databases were searched through 18 June 2026. Eligible studies assessed standalone imaging AI and supplied an exact test-set 2 × 2 table in the report or after author contact. Four pairings were analysed by bivariate meta-regression. Two reviewers applied QUADAS-3 at estimate level. Results Sixteen studies contributed 17 estimates. For disc displacement, magnetic resonance imaging input yielded pooled sensitivity 0.924 (95% CI, 0.859-0.960) and specificity 0.812 (0.709-0.885), compared with 0.765 (0.618-0.867) and 0.741 (0.592-0.850) for panoramic or cone-beam computed tomography input. The sensitivity difference was 0.159 and remained 0.152-0.198 in leave-one-out and replicate analyses; the omnibus pairing test was not significant (χ²(6) = 10.38, P = .110). Reference-standard relation and pairing partitioned the disc-displacement evidence identically. No estimate had low overall risk of bias, and several otherwise eligible estimates lacked exact published 2 × 2 data. Conclusions Sensitivity was higher when disc displacement was depicted directly on magnetic resonance imaging than when inferred from imaging that does not depict the disc. However, the cross-domain group contained only three estimates, the omnibus pairing test was not significant, and design factors were entangled. Performance should therefore be interpreted by pairing, while direct depiction versus proxy inference requires prospective testing. Advances in knowledge TMJ imaging AI performance should be interpreted in the context of the input modality-target pairing rather than as a property of the algorithm alone; exact test-set confusion matrices are essential for verification.

items.abstract: In this report, we introduce the Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and present Duo v1, a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time. The RWM treats intelligence and physical reality as equally fundamental to what constitutes a world. Existing world models largely focus on simulating the latter, leaving reasoning and decision-making as external controls rather than intrinsic parts of the world itself. In RWM, we identify two equally fundamental capabilities: Intent, which provides the cognition underlying world interactions, and Realization, which generates coherent audio-visual behavior. To realize this formulation, Duo v1 introduces three key technical designs: (1) Leveraging autoregressive modeling for continuous interaction reasoning and participation decisions, rather than restricting it to instruction understanding for diffusion models. (2) Constructing chunk-specific conditions and synchronize tokens across Intent and Realization on a unified timeline. Module-specific attention masks enforce causal dependencies both within and across chunks, preventing access to future inputs. (3) Mitigating distribution shift in both modules through dual rollout distillation, training on autoregressively generated Intent tokens and synthesized audiovisual histories from Realization. Both modules continuously perceive real-time audio, video, and text, enabling full-duplex interaction with spontaneous conversations and interruptions. Beyond conversation, users can share real objects, reshape virtual scenes, guide assistants, or play audiovisual games without mouse or keyboard controls. The release of Duo v1 makes our first step, with the next version coming soon. We look forward to broader exploration of this emerging field.

items.abstract: Introduction Synthetic biology is an emerging field that integrates engineering principles, molecular innovations, interdisciplinary methodologies, and designer toolkits to create versatile and adaptable platforms for control, enhance, and reprogram signaling, phenotype, or function in biological systems and living organisms. Advances in mammalian synthetic biology have generated growing interest in its translational applications, including cardiovascular drug discovery and disease management. Areas covered This concise report highlights promising synthetic biology-inspired technologies that have been applied or can potentially apply to transgene regulation and disease management in cardiovascular medicine, such as tunable regulatory switches, programmable gene circuits, synthetic sensing modules, and gut-heart axis engineering. We also summarize recent translational progress in the field and discuss remaining obstacles, potential solutions, and future opportunities, with particular emphasis on the progression from laboratory concepts to practical applications in cardiovascular disease. Expert opinion Synthetic biology is steadily advancing toward translation. However, barriers for clinical implementation remain, including non‑mammalian components, immunogenicity, regulatory uncertainty, and broader ethical and safety concerns. Emerging solutions, including humanized molecular components, advanced monitoring strategies, and machine learning, may help mitigate those risks and expand the cardiovascular utility of synthetic biology. Stronger evidence and deeper clinical integration will position the field for future cardiovascular medicine.

items.abstract: Alveolar echinococcosis, caused by the parasite Echinococcus multilocularis, is a potentially lethal disease that requires the development of new medical treatments. Current drug screening methods depend on manual microscopy to count stained and unstained protoscoleces to determine viability, a process that is often slow and subject to human error. This study developed machine learning models to automate the classification of protoscolex survival to accelerate drug discovery. A total of 111 images containing 1,302 protoscoleces stained with eosin or methylene blue were analyzed. Histogram-based image features were extracted and subjected to preprocessing, dimensionality reduction, and feature selection. Six classification algorithms were trained using five-fold cross-validation and evaluated on internal test sets and an external validation set via receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Results indicated that several models were highly effective, with internal test scores ranging from 0.8905 to 0.9467 and external validation scores between 0.7772 and 0.8214. Models based on support vector machine, logistic regression, and linear discriminant analysis demonstrated promising discriminatory performance across both internal and external datasets. The study concludes that machine learning can accurately and objectively classify the viability of protoscoleces based on stained images. This automated approach offers significant potential for standardizing high-throughput drug screening and facilitating the discovery of new therapeutics against this neglected zoonotic disease.

items.abstract: The scarcity of large, diverse, and unbiased protein ligand binding datasets limits the performance of machine learning approaches in drug discovery, particularly for understudied proteins. The Target 2035 initiative aims to address this gap by generating open-access binding data for more than 2,000 human proteins, a goal whose value depends on maximizing the diversity of the selected targets. Because proteins with different folds can share chemically analogous binding sites, we reasoned that pocket similarity, rather than sequence or fold similarity, is the appropriate criterion for selecting representative targets that maximize coverage of the human pocketome. Here, we use PocketVec, an alignment-free descriptor of binding sites, to map the human globular pocketome, identifying 51,535 predicted druggable pockets across 15,559 proteins. A two level hierarchical clustering, first within protein families and then across the whole proteome, grouped these pockets into 1,865 clusters of chemically similar binding sites. After discarding 533 clusters containing pockets with known ligands, we selected the 100 most populated of the remaining 1,332 ligand free clusters and chose two high quality representative pockets per cluster, ranked by their resemblance to known ligand-binding sites. Finally, we implemented two complementary prioritization strategies, one favoring structurally unexplored proteins and the other proteins amenable to experimental follow up, and selected 200 pockets from 100 different clusters from each strategy, with 89 clusters in common. Both selections cover over 10,000 pockets in ~5,600 proteins, approximately 36% of the human proteins with annotated druggable pockets, which represents a 2.8- to 4.4-fold increase in the number of covered pockets, domains, and proteins than random selection baselines. This pocket based framework offers a principled strategy to select diverse targets for Target 2035 and other large scale protein ligand data generation efforts in chemical biology.

items.abstract: RNAs are emerging as promising therapeutic targets, and small-molecule binding can modulate their structure and function, creating opportunities for therapeutic development. Accurate identification of RNA small-molecule binding sites is therefore important for understanding RNA-ligand interactions and facilitating RNA-targeted drug discovery. However, the structural complexity of RNA and the limited availability of experimentally characterized RNA-ligand complexes pose challenges for computational binding-site prediction. In this study, we propose RSMBind, a graph attention-based deep learning framework for nucleotide-level prediction of RNA-small molecule binding sites. The model integrates geometric descriptors of the local three-dimensional environment with pretrained RNA language model embeddings to capture complementary structural and sequence information. We investigate three pretrained RNA language models RNA-BERT, ERNIE-RNA and RNA-FM and assess the contributions of sequence representations and geometric features through feature-level ablation experiments. The model is developed using the TR60 and HARIBOSS datasets and evaluated on four independent benchmark datasets: RB9, TE18, TL12 and JL10. RSMBind achieves the highest MCC among the compared methods on three of the four benchmarks, with relative improvements of 17.1% on RB9, 7.2% on TL12 and 16.0% on JL10 over the best previously reported results, while achieving competitive performance on TE18. Furthermore, RSMBind retains predictive capability when using only pretrained RNA language model embeddings, highlighting their potential utility when explicit tertiary structural features are unavailable. Structural analysis indicates differences in prediction performance across RNA structural regions, with loop-associated binding sites generally being captured more effectively than those embedded within stem regions. Additionally, 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations of selected RNA-ligand complexes provide insights into the relationship between predicted binding probabilities and dynamic ligand proximity, further highlighting the role of conformational dynamics in evaluating structure-based predictions. The source code is available at [ https://github.com/sharma-nandita/RSMBind].

items.abstract: Customization and modification of machine learning derived sequences can be achieved by understanding the mechanics behind state-of-the-art protein design models such as ProteinMPNN. Uninterpretability is hypothesized to be due largely to polysemanticity where neural networks store more features than they have dimensions. Here, we introduce sparse autoencoders (SAEs) into ProteinMPNN which expand its latent space and uncovers correlations between the activations in sparse dimensions and the presence of protein features such as secondary structure, residue volume, residue shape, disulfide bridges, and coordination to ligands. Additionally, we show that sparse activations can be manipulated to produce a variant of the short chain variable fragment Brolucizumab that is more thermostable than variants produced by traditional machine learning methods based on high temperature molecular dynamics simulations. Thus, SAEs provide both mechanistic understanding of protein design models and allow customizable manipulation of sequence prediction.

items.abstract: Serpins (serine protease inhibitors) regulate proteolytic activity through a suicide-substrate inhibitory mechanism, whereby the serpin covalently traps and inactivates their target protease. Serpins are broadly conserved across eukaryotes, but the evolutionary and functional relationships between human SERPINE1, and Drosophila Serpins in incompletely defined. To identify candidate Drosophila functional analogs of SERPINE1/PAI-1, a multi-omics framework was applied to thoroughly compare the serpins across species. The multi-level analysis integrated orthology prediction, protein sequence and structural characterization, phylogenetic reconstruction, bulk tissue transcriptomics, single-cell transcriptomics, and aging-associated expression analysis. Candidate serpins (Spn42Da, Spn42Db, Spn42Dc, Spn42Dd, Spn28B, and Spn28F) were evaluated using DIOPT, AlphaFold/ChimeraX structural comparisons, reactive center loop analyses, phylogenetic distances, GTEx, Human Protein Atlas, FlyAtlas2, Fly Cell Atlas, and Aging Fly Cell Atlas datasets. Comparative analyses demonstrated full-length sequence and reactive center loop (RCL) divergence despite preservation of the canonical serpin fold. Tissue, cell-type, and age-associated expression analysis revealed distinct candidate-specific patterns. Spn42Dd comparisons uncovered similarities to human SERPINE1 in sequence/structural and broad expression but did not represent the strongest overall cross-species expression correlations. Spn42Da and Spn42Db received the highest cross species integrated support. Quality check of the ranking confirmed that Spn42Da and Spn42Db were stable top candidates across orthology, sequence alignment, and expression domains. The multi-domain analysis was unable to identify a single definitive Drosophila serpin as the closest counterpart to human SERPINE1, indicating that cross-species similarity is distributed across multiple candidate serpins. This study therefore provides a quantitative method for prioritizing potential evolutionary and functional analogs across highly divergent species.

items.abstract: Accurate, rapid, and standardized interpretation of multiparametric flow cytometry findings is essential for clinical decision-making in patients evaluated for suspected acute leukemia. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of ChatGPT, a general-purpose large language model, in interpreting de-identified, laboratory-generated flow cytometry graphical outputs from patients with suspected acute leukemia and to assess its agreement with the consensus interpretation of two hematologists in terms of diagnostic classification, blast percentage estimation, and hematogone detection. This retrospective observational validation study included 560 patients who underwent bone marrow aspiration and flow cytometric immunophenotyping during their initial diagnostic evaluation for suspected acute leukemia. All included patients were undergoing initial diagnostic evaluation and had neither a previous diagnosis of leukemia nor prior leukemia-directed treatment. The consensus diagnosis established by two hematologists was considered the reference standard. Between May 4 and 15, 2026, de-identified, laboratory-generated PDF images containing flow cytometry dot plots from a three-tube acute leukemia panel comprising 28 antibody-fluorochrome combinations were uploaded directly through the ChatGPT Plus web interface and interpreted using GPT-5.5 (OpenAI). Raw FCS files were not provided. Using the same standardized prompt for each case, the model was asked to estimate the blast percentage, select a single most likely diagnosis from five predefined categories (no pathology, MDS, AML, B-ALL, or T-ALL), and determine the presence or absence of hematogones. The initial response for each case was archived and directly encoded without adjudication. Diagnosis-specific performance was evaluated using one-versus-rest sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, accuracy, and F1-score. Overall agreement between ChatGPT-generated classifications and hematologist consensus was assessed using Cohen's kappa. Pearson's correlation coefficient was used to evaluate the association between blast percentage estimates, whereas Bland-Altman analysis was used to quantify agreement, systematic bias, and 95% limits of agreement. Hematogone detection was evaluated as a binary classification task using sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy. ChatGPT achieved an overall diagnostic accuracy of 78.8% (95% CI, 75.2%-81.9%), with substantial agreement with hematologist consensus (Cohen's κ = 0.712; 95% CI, 0.664-0.757). Diagnosis-specific sensitivity ranged from 69.2% to 87.3%, and PPV ranged from 60.0% to 93.5%. The highest sensitivity was observed for MDS, whereas the highest PPV was observed for no pathology. McNemar's test identified significant systematic differences between ChatGPT and hematologist classifications for no pathology (p = 0.041), AML (p = 0.008), and T-ALL (p = 0.023). Blast percentage estimates were strongly correlated (Pearson's r = 0.818; 95% CI, 0.789-0.844; p< 0.001); however, Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated a mean positive bias of 3.92 percentage points, indicating systematic overestimation by ChatGPT. For hematogone detection, ChatGPT achieved an accuracy of 89.5%, sensitivity of 70.3%, and specificity of 92.4%. ChatGPT-based flow cytometry interpretation showed promise for preliminary diagnostic classification and quality assurance applications. However, expert hematologist validation remains essential, particularly in scenarios associated with high diagnostic consequences, including AML and T-ALL classification, blast percentage estimation, and accurate discrimination of hematogones.

items.abstract: Integrating multimodal data is essential to advance neuroscience as a discipline. Large-scale collaborative efforts, exemplified by the BRAIN Initiative, together with advances in single-cell and spatial omics, multimodal imaging, human genetics, behavioral phenotyping, protein structure prediction, and related technologies, are transforming neuroscience into a data-rich, highly interconnected science. As experimental resources, scientific literature, and collaborative networks continue to expand, integrating discoveries across modalities, species, and levels of biological organization has become the field's central bottleneck. This Perspective argues that artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming essential for overcoming these constraints. Using six evolving approaches we outline strategies to accelerate AI adoption through community building and pilot projects that drive AI transformation at both the organizational and technological levels. Organizational transformation cultivates broad AI awareness and a pro-AI culture while technological transformation improves the efficiency, scalability, and quality of data analysis, allowing researchers to generate insights more rapidly and effectively. Together, these advances position AI as a key driver for advancing neuroscience at scale.

items.abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) are central to many biological processes, but their function depends on dynamic conformational ensembles rather than a single structure. Despite the impact of artificial intelligence on protein structure prediction, determining these ensembles at atomistic resolution remains challenging. Recently, we introduced bAIes, a framework that leverages the structural information encoded in AlphaFold2 distograms to generate conformational ensembles of IDPs at atomistic resolution. Here, we extend this framework to six state-of-the-art structure prediction tools (AlphaFold2, AlphaFold3, Boltz-1, Boltz-2, ESMFold, and ESMFold2) and systematically compare the structural information encoded in their predicted inter-residue distance distributions. Despite differences between predictors, we show that bAIes generates ensembles with comparable accuracy against experimental NMR and SAXS data, and competitive performance relative to state-of-the-art all-atom simulations and alternative IDP ensemble generation methods. These results demonstrate that bAIes is robust to the choice of structure predictor and that the distance distributions generated by different deep learning architectures contain valuable information about the conformational preferences of disordered proteins. More broadly, our work highlights the potential of combining AI-derived structural information with physics-based modeling to generate atomistic ensembles of intrinsically disordered proteins and regions.
