items.abstract: Coding agents combine visual understanding with program execution, offering a new route to automated 3D creation. By translating images and instructions into editable programs, they bring reconstruction, generation, and editing into a shared workflow. Yet existing benchmarks fragment evaluation across task scopes and protocols, leaving their capabilities across construction levels unclear. We propose Frontier3DBench, a unified benchmark of 145 tasks across 9 categories spanning object, scene, and interactive open-world creation, with joint evaluation of appearance, structure, and behavior. Experiments with 11 model-harness configurations reveal strengths that vary by level: GPT-6.1-sol leads the object and scene levels and achieves the highest overall score of 66.02/100, whereas GPT-6-astra leads interactive world construction. However, all configurations score lower on reference reconstruction than on text-driven generation in object and scene tasks. Producing plausible content thus remains easier than reproducing specified geometry, layouts, and visual details. Moreover, generated worlds average 83.08/100 on local mechanisms but only 20.82 on motion clearance and 30.26 on stateful workflows: individual mechanisms often function, whereas complete activities that require coordinated actions and persistent state remain difficult. These results identify reference fidelity and coordinated activity completion as central bottlenecks for coding agents in 3D creation.

items.title: OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling
items.summary: 3D part decomposition is a central capability for editable asset creation, yet existing workflows typically segment a completed mesh as a post-processing step, making the result sensitive to geometric artifacts, texture ambiguity, and limited part-level annotations. We present OmniLatent, a unified latent modeling framework for 3D part decomposition. Instead of predicting part labels in isolation, OmniLatent learns…
items.abstract: 3D part decomposition is a central capability for editable asset creation, yet existing workflows typically segment a completed mesh as a post-processing step, making the result sensitive to geometric artifacts, texture ambiguity, and limited part-level annotations. We present OmniLatent, a unified latent modeling framework for 3D part decomposition. Instead of predicting part labels in isolation, OmniLatent learns a shared latent space that jointly encodes geometry, deformation, appearance, and binary part IDs, allowing data-rich geometric and visual priors to support data-scarce part learning. Given a single input image, the base model generates geometry, deformation, texture, and surface part IDs in one pass, producing a part-aware 3D asset without a separate segmentation stage. We further tune the pretrained model for two extensions: a point-prompt adapter that maps arbitrary 3D point prompts with binary part IDs into latent tokens for full segmentation, refinement, and part subdivision, and an amodal part completion model that completes partial surface masks into a coherent full-object decomposition through dynamic per-part token allocation, cross-attention to the given geometry latent, and alternating part-local and global attention. Extensive experiments show that OmniLatent produces semantically meaningful part segmentations with precise boundaries, supports interactive part editing, and completes partial part observations while preserving global object consistency.

items.title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
items.summary: Recent years have witnessed remarkable progress in video generation in terms of visual quality and temporal consistency. However, generating videos with precise spatial structure, coherent motion dynamics, and controllable scene composition remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce Video-Coder, the first attempt to train a code-driven video generation agent, which autonomously writes and executes code to…
items.abstract: Recent years have witnessed remarkable progress in video generation in terms of visual quality and temporal consistency. However, generating videos with precise spatial structure, coherent motion dynamics, and controllable scene composition remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce Video-Coder, the first attempt to train a code-driven video generation agent, which autonomously writes and executes code to construct a dynamic 3D scene (Draft Video) that provides structure and motion signals to downstream video generators. To support this paradigm, we design a dedicated data pipeline and curate two high-quality datasets, Video-Coder-SFT-6k and Video-Coder-RL-2k, which contain diverse prompts and ground-truth reference videos. We further develop the Video- Coder Harness, a unified interactive environment integrating code execution, 3D scene rendering, and execution feedback for agent training and inference. We then train Video-Coder with SFT fol- lowed by harness-native agentic reinforcement learning with dual reward feedback, which combines execution-based and video-based rewards. Additionally, we design an annealing training strategy that gradually reduces the execution reward over time, allowing the model to rely more on the video reward in the later training stages. Experiments show that Video-Coder achieves significant gains, improving Minimax-H3 by approximately 7 points on PhyGenBench and 24 points on VBench-2.0. We hope this work can serve as an open foundation for coding agents in video generation, and we fully open-source our data, models, and code

items.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
items.summary: Weight-Space Programming (WSP) enables reasoning agents to directly inspect and modify neural network parameters, offering an alternative to gradient-based model adaptation. However, its capabilities, cross-task generalization, and practical limitations remain insufficiently understood. We systematically investigate WSP through 16 editing trajectories across seven benchmarks and two model scales (Qwen3.5-0.8B and…
items.abstract: Weight-Space Programming (WSP) enables reasoning agents to directly inspect and modify neural network parameters, offering an alternative to gradient-based model adaptation. However, its capabilities, cross-task generalization, and practical limitations remain insufficiently understood. We systematically investigate WSP through 16 editing trajectories across seven benchmarks and two model scales (Qwen3.5-0.8B and Qwen3.5-9B). Our findings reveal three key insights. First, WSP can achieve substantial performance gains through highly localized interventions. On full held-out evaluations, accuracy improves by up to 29.45, 4.42, 36.72, and 17.11 percentage points on MATH-500, GPQA Diamond, IFEval, and SciBench, respectively. Notably, modifying only 1,023 parameters yields a 29.45-point improvement. Second, WSP exhibits promising but uneven cross-task generalization. A Math-edited checkpoint improves GPQA Diamond, IFEval, and SciBench by 3.03, 12.18, and 20.10 points, respectively, without further editing, while leaving SciCode performance unchanged. Third, effective editing remains challenging and inconsistent. Outcomes vary substantially across trajectories, and six of the 16 trajectories retain the original weights when candidate improvements cannot be reliably validated. Together, these results highlight WSP's potential for highly localized model adaptation while revealing important challenges in intervention discovery, reliability, and cross-task transfer. Homepage: https://wsp-scope.github.io/ GitHub: https://github.com/WSP-Scope/WSP-Scope-Project

items.title: SIRIS: Can LLMs Tell When Simulation Errors Matter in AI-Driven Systems Research
items.summary: LLM agents increasingly drive systems research and rely on simulators to evaluate candidate designs at scale. Simulators are imperfect by design: their modeling limitations can distort predictions yet leave the recommended design correct, or change which design should be selected. We introduce Siris to test whether LLMs can tell these cases apart, judging from their systems understanding when a limitation…
items.abstract: LLM agents increasingly drive systems research and rely on simulators to evaluate candidate designs at scale. Simulators are imperfect by design: their modeling limitations can distort predictions yet leave the recommended design correct, or change which design should be selected. We introduce Siris to test whether LLMs can tell these cases apart, judging from their systems understanding when a limitation invalidates the simulator's recommendation. By perturbing a simulator, Siris constructs workload pairs with the same candidates, limitation, and simulator recommendation. The perturbation changes predictions on both workloads, yet a reference simulator supports the recommendation on only one. Evaluating thirteen frontier LLMs on LLM serving design problems, we find that identifying a limitation does not ensure a correct choice, and even the strongest models sometimes abandon valid recommendations. Self-correction through a review turn helps these models restore valid choices but introduces new errors in several others. These findings motivate evaluating systems understanding through design decisions under imperfect simulators.

items.title: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence
items.summary: Foundation models increasingly guide robot actions, yet sustained autonomy requires efficient control and failure recovery. We introduce A2-MEAS, an embodied multi-agent framework built around code as a scaling interface. Learned correction codes combine corrective language, spatial evidence, execution history, and action proposals. MetaBrain provides training supervision and runtime guidance. A correction encoder…
items.abstract: Foundation models increasingly guide robot actions, yet sustained autonomy requires efficient control and failure recovery. We introduce A2-MEAS, an embodied multi-agent framework built around code as a scaling interface. Learned correction codes combine corrective language, spatial evidence, execution history, and action proposals. MetaBrain provides training supervision and runtime guidance. A correction encoder and adapter absorb this knowledge into policy weights during training, while fresh codes adapt behavior with frozen weights at deployment. The action model, A2-WLA, adds motion-aware history and a latent world model to a vision-language-action policy. Surprisingly, this simple design with action pretraining and task specialization reaches 0.5755 Q-score on the 50-task BEHAVIOR 2026 public subset before online correction, 2.21x the 2025 winner's reported 0.2605 across different benchmark editions and training configurations. On all 100 BEHAVIOR 2026 public tasks, A2-MEAS achieves 0.6411 Q-score and 45.40% task success. On RoboTwin 2.0, A2-WLA achieves 93.98% average success, rising to 95.05% with the complete system. Across 12 real-robot tasks in five household settings, A2-WLA achieves 57.92% average success versus 26.67% for pi0.5. In long-horizon pour-over coffee preparation, a history-conditioned adapter raises post-failure completion at two filter-handling steps from 14% to 94% and from 8% to 82%, compared with A2-WLA retries. Our training infrastructure delivers 427.1 samples per second, 4.03x the throughput of a pi0.5 reference implementation on matched hardware. We will release the system, models, training scripts, and infrastructure to support efficient embodied learning.

items.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
items.summary: Large language models reinvent the wheel all the time. They conflate task-solving with the execution of the solutions, which forces them to solve every problem from scratch. We show that once a task has been reasoned through, the application of its solution to a new problem instance can be done very efficiently and with little involvement from language models. We introduce agentic reasoning caching, a method for…
items.abstract: Large language models reinvent the wheel all the time. They conflate task-solving with the execution of the solutions, which forces them to solve every problem from scratch. We show that once a task has been reasoned through, the application of its solution to a new problem instance can be done very efficiently and with little involvement from language models. We introduce agentic reasoning caching, a method for constructing robust CPU-executable agentic reasoning caches (ARCs) from LLM reasoning traces. ARCs show on-par performance with frontier LLMs across a range of difficult mathematical and scientific tasks, are fully explainable, continually trainable, robust to input perturbations, and 16-291x cheaper to invoke than the source model.

items.title: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters
items.summary: Language model deployment often requires different trade-offs between competing objectives as user preferences change, yet standard post-training methods typically produce a single policy for a fixed objective weighting. We introduce LambdaMix, a new parameter efficient method for learning a preference conditioned family of policies with group-relative online reinforcement learning. LambdaMix jointly trains one…
items.abstract: Language model deployment often requires different trade-offs between competing objectives as user preferences change, yet standard post-training methods typically produce a single policy for a fixed objective weighting. We introduce LambdaMix, a new parameter efficient method for learning a preference conditioned family of policies with group-relative online reinforcement learning. LambdaMix jointly trains one low-rank adapter per objective over a frozen base model. One preference vector selects the adapter mixture that generates responses and weights the separately normalized rewards used to update the adapters. A single training run supports changing preferences at inference without further optimization. We experiment with four models on helpfulness and harmlessness and on solving math problems while following instructions. We also evaluate the two largest models on rewriting comments to preserve wording while reducing clues about personal attributes. On the first two tasks, LambdaMix achieves higher hypervolume than all evaluated conditioned and policy merging baselines across all four models. LambdaMix uses fewer training completions and stores fewer adapter parameters than a set of GRPO specialist policies. With architecture and initialization fixed, varying adapter mixtures and objective weights together gives wider score ranges and higher coverage than varying either alone.

items.title: Utilising digital technologies for mycetoma management: A comprehensive review of advances and opportunities.
items.summary: Mycetoma is a neglected tropical disease characterised by chronic, destructive infections of subcutaneous tissues, predominantly affecting populations in endemic regions with limited healthcare resources. Delayed diagnosis, limited treatment options, and restricted access to specialised healthcare contribute to substantial morbidity, disability, and socioeconomic burden. Digital technologies offer promising…
items.abstract: Mycetoma is a neglected tropical disease characterised by chronic, destructive infections of subcutaneous tissues, predominantly affecting populations in endemic regions with limited healthcare resources. Delayed diagnosis, limited treatment options, and restricted access to specialised healthcare contribute to substantial morbidity, disability, and socioeconomic burden. Digital technologies offer promising opportunities to address these challenges and improve mycetoma care. Artificial intelligence (AI) can support early detection and diagnostic accuracy through the analysis of clinical images, radiological findings, and patient data. Telemedicine can facilitate remote specialist consultations and follow-up, particularly in rural and underserved communities, while electronic health records enable systematic data collection, disease surveillance, and monitoring of treatment outcomes. Mobile health applications can improve patient education, symptom monitoring, and treatment adherence, whereas computational drug discovery may accelerate the identification of potential therapeutic agents. Furthermore, digital platforms can strengthen international research collaborations, knowledge exchange, and capacity building. However, implementing these technologies in endemic regions faces significant barriers, including inadequate digital infrastructure, limited internet connectivity, insufficient digital literacy, data privacy concerns, and ethical challenges related to informed consent, data ownership, and algorithmic decision-making. Addressing these barriers requires investment in infrastructure, appropriate regulatory frameworks, stakeholder collaboration, and context-specific capacity-building initiatives. Integrating digital health solutions into national healthcare strategies could support sustainable and equitable improvements in mycetoma management. This review highlights the potential applications, opportunities, and challenges of digital technologies in mycetoma care and emphasises the need for inclusive, locally adapted approaches to enhance early diagnosis, treatment outcomes, research, and health equity in endemic communities.

items.abstract: Diethyl phthalate (DEP) is a ubiquitous environmental endocrine-disrupting chemical to which human populations are widely exposed. Increasing evidence links DEP to the malignant progression of solid tumors; however, the key molecular networks and experimentally validated mechanisms underlying DEP-enhanced invasion in gastric cancer (GC) remain largely undefined. Four transcriptomic datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus were integrated to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs), followed by weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) to determine tumor-associated key modules. Potential DEP targets were predicted using multiple databases and intersected with-related DEGs and key module genes to define core candidate genes. Functional enrichment and network analyses were then performed. Subsequently, a multi-model ensemble machine learning framework combined with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based interpretability was applied to prioritize candidate genes. Molecular docking was used to evaluate the potential binding affinity between DEP and key target proteins. Finally, the effects of DEP on oxidative stress, migration and invasion, cytoskeletal remodeling, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) were experimentally validated in AGS and HGC-27 cells. Thirteen core candidate genes were identified. Functional enrichment analyses primarily implicated lysosomal proteolysis, extracellular matrix remodeling, and chromatin remodeling and epigenetic regulation. Among the evaluated machine learning models, the gradient boosting machine (GBM) model demonstrated the best overall diagnostic performance. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis of an additional random forest model highlighted CTSB, PLAU, ALDH3A1, ATAD2, and CBX7 as influential features for GC classification. Molecular docking predicted potential interactions between DEP and these candidate proteins. In vitro experiments demonstrated that DEP exposure increased intracellular reactive oxygen species levels and promoted cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in AGS and HGC-27 cells. These effects were accompanied by filamentous actin (F-actin) reorganization, increased RhoA and MLC1 expression, decreased E-cadherin expression, and increased N-cadherin and vimentin expression, consistent with EMT-related alterations. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that DEP exposure enhances invasion-related malignant phenotypes in gastric cancer cells and identify candidate molecular targets potentially associated with GC progression. Although network toxicology, machine learning, and molecular docking provide complementary evidence for target prioritization, further functional studies are required to determine whether these candidate targets directly mediate DEP-induced cellular effects.

items.abstract: The quantitative measurement of mitochondrial stress from fluorescence images of cells remains a challenging task. Existing methods rely on mitochondrial segmentation, manually predefined features, and discrete phenotype severity classes, which are prone to error and bias. Here, we present MitoDecode, a deep learning network that automatically assesses type and severity of mitochondrial stress from fluorescence microscopy images. MitoDecode eliminates the need for mitochondrial segmentation, is parameter-free, and operates across both diffraction-limited and super-resolution optical imaging modalities. It assigns a phenotypic probability profile for each individual cell, indicating both type and severity of phenotypic stress. The readout thus enables comparisons between different stressors and provides clues for underlying mechanisms. Furthermore, the method captures phenotypic shifts continuously across treatment doses, revealing subtle variations that would otherwise be missed. We demonstrate MitoDecode’s adaptability across diverse cell types, imaging modalities, and stress conditions, and show that it can reliably detect mitochondrial phenotypes, even when stressors target non-mitochondrial pathways. We validate the reliability of the model with biochemical assays, showcase its utility for phenotypic stress profiling of drug treatments, and envisage its application for early-stage disease detection, drug discovery, and mechanistic lead generation.

items.abstract: Olfaction-based biosensors stand to have profound impacts in fields such as medical diagnostics, national security, and drug discovery. A promising mode of vapor phase biodetection mimics volatile organic compound-olfactory receptor (VOC-OR) interactions with target-specific protein or peptide probes; however, lack of experimental coverage remains a core bottleneck. Current computational approaches aim to improve prediction of VOC-OR binding to reduce experimental burden, and current machine learning approaches fail to demonstrate a level of generalization that addresses current engineering challenges. Here, using the Molecular to Olfactory Dataset (M2OR) and Insect Olfactory Binding Protein Database (iOBPdb) datasets, data partitioning methods and their performance are evaluated on a neural network and contrastive learning framework on such VOC-OR binding datasets, varying: model training, architecture, and structure of the input data distribution. It was found that holding out certain chemical or proteomic motifs from the training data diminished model performance with a two layer neural network model. The model was able to generalize to state of the art performance (0.88 AUCROC) on every data split by applying a contrastive learning objective defined by shared molecular constituents and a stochastic sampler. This suggests the contrastive objective provides a strong inductive bias for neural networks to predict novel VOC-OR pairs. These findings highlight that model performance on pairwise biological interaction datasets can be inflated through identity leakage from constituent overlap, and emphasize the need for more robust evaluation protocols. Furthermore, we show contrastive regularization mitigates dataset degeneracy through enforcement of compatibility in the models latent geometry that may extend to other binder target-datasets where identity leakage confounds evaluation.

items.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming of myeloid‑derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) plays a role in immunotherapy resistance in colorectal cancer (CRC). This metabolic reprogramming appears to be coordinated by oncogenic mutations (such as adenomatous polyposis coli, KRAS and TP53) through a proposed self‑reinforcing 'mutation‑metabolism‑suppression' axis. In the present review, four core metabolic pillars sustaining MDSC pathogenicity and the epimetabolic regulation that durably locks them into a suppressive state were examined. Furthermore, two emerging dimensions were highlighted: The spatial metabolic antagonism through which MDSCs may construct a metabolically hostile zone to limit the functional activity of tertiary lymphoid structures, and the remote manipulation of MDSC function by gut and intratumoral microbiota‑derived metabolites. To transcend the limitations of non‑specific myeloid depletion, immunometabolic rehabilitation is proposed as a potentially transformative framework targeting intrinsic metabolic vulnerabilities to functionally reprogram MDSCs from an immunosuppressive to a homeostatic or immunostimulatory phenotype. By integrating emerging spatial omics for precise target validation, artificial intelligence‑guided rational drug design and microbiome modulation, this paradigm provides a strategic roadmap for next‑generation precision immunotherapy, aiming to achieve durable responses across both microsatellite stable and microsatellite instability‑high CRC.

items.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have expanded treatment options across multiple malignancies, but their clinical benefit remains constrained by heterogeneous and sometimes serious toxicities. These toxicities rarely arise from a single component; instead, they reflect the association between target biology, molecular architecture, systemic exposure, and tissue susceptibility. We first examine the structural basis of ADC toxicity by discussing the distinct contributions of the antibody-target axis, linker, payload, drug loading, and conjugation strategy to systemic exposure and tissue toxicity. We distinguish organ-selective "on-target, off-tumor" injury from target-independent toxicity and further characterize two major off-target routes: context-dependent uptake of intact ADCs through Fcγ receptor-mediated or pinocytosis-dominant pathways, and spatially distinct exposure to released payload arising from premature systemic release or localized bystander diffusion. Furthermore, we summarize a multidisciplinary management framework, ranging from prophylactic measures to graded interventions across complex scenarios such as treatment rechallenge and combination therapy. Finally, we discuss strategies to widen the therapeutic window through exposure-response-guided dosing, next-generation molecular engineering, and emerging conjugate platforms. Artificial intelligence and computational approaches may further extend safety optimization from drug design to patient stratification and real-world surveillance. By linking molecular design, spatial exposure, and clinical management, this review provides an integrated framework to improve ADC safety while preserving antitumor efficacy.

items.abstract: The preoperative prediction of clinically relevant postoperative pancreatic fistula (CR-POPF) is crucial for the implementation of efficient prevention strategies in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Our study aimed to explore the value of habitat imaging employing virtual magnetic resonance elastography (vMRE) and continuous-time random-walk (CTRW) diffusion MRI for preoperatively predicting CR-POPF in PDAC after pancreaticoduodenectomy. vMRE reflected pancreatic stiffness, whereas CTRW-derived parameters characterized non-Gaussian water diffusion and microstructural heterogeneity. Their voxel-wise integration could identify imaging-defined phenotype reflecting complementary tissue properties. Patients with suspected PDAC who underwent pancreatic MRI were prospectively collected. Multiple-b-value diffusion-weighted imaging sequence was acquired and fitted to CTRW model. The diffusion-based tissue shear modulus (μ diff ) was calculated by calibrating the shifted apparent diffusion coefficient (sADC) with standard MR elastography (MRE). The presumed pancreatic stump was segmented into various subregions by habitat analysis employing two combinations of vMRE and CTRW parameter maps. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify the independent factors and construct the prediction models. The predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve and validated using bootstrap method. A total of 183 patients were finally included, and 36 patients (19.67%) developed CR-POPF. The optimism-corrected area under the curve (AUC) of two combined models was 0.947 (95% CI, 0.898-0.987) and 0.897 (95% CI, 0.832-0.962) respectively, through bootstrap validation. Habitat analysis using vMRE and CTRW diffusion model provided complementary characterization of stiffness and diffusion heterogeneity, and exhibited great potential for the preoperative prediction of CR-POPF in PDAC after pancreaticoduodenectomy.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems for chest X-ray (CXR) interpretation can detect abnormalities, generate reports, provide visual grounding, and support dialogue but often offer limited mechanisms for inspection and follow-up. We present Transparent Radiology Assistance for Chest X-ray Explanation and Review (TRACER), a multimodal multi-agent workflow integrating CXR analysis, consultation support, and prior-report comparison with structured findings, gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) cues, report-generation steps, and execution trajectories. Evaluation included report-quality benchmarking on 2000 frontal CXRs and user studies with 60 non-radiologist participants. Experiment II used 12 cases, with one fixed report per case in both text-only and transparency-supported conditions; the latter additionally displayed structured findings, finding-specific Grad-CAM cues, and execution trajectories. Open-ended responses were scored by an independent automated judge with clinician validation on a stratified subset. Experiment III evaluated eight prior-current pairs with or without an archive-assisted comparison paragraph. The full report pipeline achieved the best values on six of eight automatic metrics. Transparency support increased Consultation Preparation Quality from 2.133 ± 1.302 to 3.142 ± 1.154 (odds ratio 6.76, 95% confidence interval 3.92-11.67; P<0.001 ). Archive assistance improved difference identification from 0.642±0.338 to 0.833±0.285 (odds ratio 4.16, 95% confidence interval 2.33-7.42; P<0.001 ) and reduced mean completion time from 108.825 to 74.225 s. The transparency-supported condition also yielded higher usability ratings and lower perceived workload. These findings support TRACER as an inspectable workflow for CXR report review, verification-oriented consultation preparation, and prior-current comparison; clinical usefulness requires evaluation with patients and clinicians.

items.abstract: Lumbar spinal stenosis (LSS) is a prevalent degenerative condition and a major cause of disability in aging populations. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the preferred modality for assessment; however, severity grading remains inconsistent across readers and institutions, limiting reproducibility and complicating clinical decision-making. This study presents LSS-Net, a two-stage deep learning framework for automated grading of central canal stenosis using sagittal T2-weighted MRI. The first stage performs vertebral localization using a single-stage object detector, enabling standardized extraction of intervertebral regions of interest. The second stage applies a Swin Transformer-based classifier to predict stenosis severity (Normal/Mild, Moderate, Severe). The framework was developed using a multi-center dataset of 1,975 studies and evaluated on a held-out subset. Vertebral localization achieved 97.9% F1-score, while severity classification reached a weighted F1-score of 77.1%. Performance was highest for Normal/Mild and Severe classes, with reduced accuracy observed in Moderate cases, reflecting known diagnostic ambiguity. External clinical validation was conducted on an independent dataset using two expert readers. The model demonstrated substantial agreement with a neurosurgeon (accuracy 75.1%, κ=0.73 ) and moderate agreement with a neuroradiologist (accuracy 51.0%, κ=0.56 ), with inter-expert agreement in a comparable range. These findings suggest that LSS-Net may support more consistent and reproducible LSS grading. However, performance limitations in borderline cases and the restricted use of single-slice sagittal input highlight the need for further validation and extension to multi-sequence and multi-compartment analysis before clinical deployment.

items.abstract: 18F-FDG (18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose)-PET/computed tomography (CT) has emerged as a pivotal molecular imaging modality that extends beyond diagnosis to influence therapeutic decision-making in infectious and inflammatory diseases. By detecting increased glucose metabolism in activated inflammatory cells, it enables whole-body visualization of active disease before structural abnormalities become apparent on conventional imaging. Quantitative parameters support reproducible longitudinal monitoring. Its incorporation into international guidelines highlights its growing role in precision-guided management. Emerging technologies, including digital and long axial field-of-view PET/CT, artificial intelligence, radiomics, PET/MR imaging, and pathogen-specific or immune cell-specific tracers, may further enhance diagnostic accuracy and personalized treatment.

items.abstract: The nuclear entry of the capsid protein is a critical step in the life cycle of circoviruses, but whether capsid proteins from different circoviruses differ in their importin interactions remained unclear. Here, we modeled 298 unique circovirus capsid protein-importin pairs using AlphaFold 3. After conformational clustering and ZDOCK concordance filtering, 603 representative interfaces were retained for analysis. We extracted Δ iG values, interface features, and nuclear localization signal (NLS)-specific interface properties by PDBePISA and analyzed them with statistical tests. Capsid protein (Cap)-importin-9 (IPO9) complexes showed the lowest mean Δ iG among all tested circoviruses, identifying IPO9 as a candidate broadly interacting importin among the viruses examined. Across all host classes, Cap-importin β complexes showed a lower mean Δ iG than Cap-importin α or Cap-transportin complexes. Predicted Δ iG patterns differed across host classes, with distinct profiles for avian, mammalian, and fish circoviruses. Predicted Δ iG patterns and NLS interface features, including basic residue ratio, interface occupancy, and net charge, differed across avian, mammalian, and fish circoviruses. Together, these results provide a set of testable predictions regarding circovirus Cap-importin interfaces and highlight the predicted NLS interface as a region for further investigation.

items.abstract: Bacterial proteins are specialized with extensive functional diversity for survival in diverse and stressful environments. A significant portion of these proteins remains functionally uncharacterized, limiting our understanding of bacterial survival mechanisms. Hence, we develop Deep Expression STructure (DeepEST), a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts protein function in bacteria by assigning Gene Ontology (GO) terms. DeepEST comprises two modules: a multi-layer perceptron that uses gene expression and gene location, and a protein structure-based module that uses predicted structures and amino acid sequences. Within DeepEST, we integrate these modules through a learnable weighted linear combination and introduce a novel masked loss function to fine-tune the structure-based predictor for bacterial species. These choices are well suited for bacteria, in which functionally related genes frequently colocalize and are cotranscribed within operons, allowing transcription dynamics to serve as informative, condition-dependent signals. We show that DeepEST outperforms existing protein function prediction methods on a 25-species benchmark, relying solely on amino acid sequence or protein structure. Averaged over the 25 species, DeepEST reaches a protein-centric F max of 0.689 and a term-centric micro-AUPRC of 0.756, a relative improvement of 4.4% and 11.6% over the second-best method, the structure-based predictor DeepFRI. Moreover, DeepEST predicts GO terms for unclassified hypothetical proteins across 25 human bacterial pathogens, supporting their experimental characterization. DeepEST bridges organism-specific data integration and structure-based transfer learning, providing a method tailored for bacterial protein function prediction in settings with structural and multi-condition expression data.

items.abstract: Bicaudal-C (Bicc1) is an essential cell-fate regulator that guides the animal body plan during early development and maintains organ homeostasis in adults. It does so by binding specific mRNA targets and regulating their translation, yet the molecular basis of mRNA target selection has remained unclear. Here, we combined experimental and computational approaches to define the Bicc1-RNA interaction. In vitro binding experiments with wild-type and mutant RNA substrates identified the RNA features recognized by Bicc1, while protein-RNA XL-MS-a UV-crosslinking approach coupled to LC-MS/MS-pinpointed Bicc1 amino acids in direct contact with RNA. Deep protein-sequence alignments showed that key RNA contacts are conserved across invertebrates and vertebrates, and binding experiments with recombinant Bicc1 proteins from multiple species confirmed this conservation functionally. AlphaFold 3.0 predictions of Bicc1-RNA complexes generated a structural model that complemented and extended these experimental findings. Together, these data establish that Bicc1 recognizes a bipartite binding site comprising a GAC primary sequence and a stem-loop structure through contacts distributed across both the KH1 and KH2 domains. This interface is conserved from invertebrates to vertebrates. This work thus defines the evolutionarily conserved mechanism by which Bicc1 selects specific mRNAs for translational regulation.

items.abstract: Large-genome bacteriophages (phages) of the Chimalliviridae family have a distinctive life cycle, building compartments inside infected bacterial cells that broadly protect their genomes from host defenses. Here, we use cryo-electron microscopy to determine a structure of the Escherichia coli -infecting Chimalliviridae phage Goslar. We combine manual modeling of 25 structural proteins with AlphaFold structure predictions of an additional three proteins to generate a composite model with 2888 protein chains from 28 different structural proteins, totaling more than 1.4 million amino acid residues. Our structure reveals the architecture of the Goslar capsid, portal, tail, and baseplate, highlighting structural similarities and differences with other tailed phages. Combining our structural data with quantitative mass spectrometry of Goslar virions, we identify several high-copy virion-associated proteins that likely play key roles when injected into host cells upon infection. We also identify a Chimalliviridae -specific family of proteins that form long, flexible filaments anchored at the phage baseplate and which incorporate carbohydrate-binding domains, suggesting a key role in host recognition.

items.abstract: Protein complexes carry out critical functions during development. Mapping cell-type-specific protein complexes in early embryogenesis is essential for uncovering the molecular mechanisms of embryonic development. We unfortunately currently lack a catalog of protein complexes specific for embryogenesis including embryonic stem cells. Here we develop a proteomics-based machine learning workflow to predict protein complexes present in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESC). Our method integrates data from a cell-type agnostic protein complex resource with co-fractionation mass spectrometry (CF-MS) experiments on mESC. Our resource, stem.MAP, identifies 3,986 complexes encompassing ~133,000 unique interactions, and 8,616 proteins. stem.MAP captures variant complexes critical for stem cell function including the PRC2, BAF and NuRD complexes. stem.MAP also discriminates mutually exclusive interactions specific to embryonic stem cells (e.g. Eif4ebp2 - Eif4e). Finally we observe 1,388 high confidence stem.MAP interactions found only in mESC CF-MS data, many with support from AlphaFold modeling and a gastruloid coregulation network. We make stem.MAP protein complexes available through our web resource: stem.proteincomplexes.org. We anticipate stem.MAP will be beneficial to the study of early development and we expect our proteomics-based machine learning workflow to be applicable to the creation of any context-specific protein interaction network.

items.abstract: The Evolutionary Classification of Domains (ECOD) organizes protein domains into a hierarchy of evolutionary relationships, encompassing both experimentally determined and computationally predicted structures. ECOD now classifies 2.9M domains, of which ∼1.37M derived from the Protein Data Bank and 1.51M from predicted models in the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database. The principal development we report here is a complete rebuild of the ECOD web resource. Search has been reconstructed around three modalities: (i) sequence, (ii) structure, and (iii) keyword. Foldseek now is the primary search method for the ECOD web page, searching a ∼457k representative domain database that is also distributed for local use. Results are presented through a Mol* interactive viewer, and a new API has been developed for programmatic access to the database. Alongside the interface, the pipeline for classifying new PDB entries has been rebuilt and returned to a regular cadence, family groups have been synchronized with Pfam v38.2, the bulk distributables have been reorganized and now include the search databases, the ligands in contact with each domain are recorded for experimental structures and annotated with drug cross-references from DrugDomain, and a registry has been introduced through which ECOD assigns stable identifiers to gene-called proteins and records the structures it predicts. ECOD is freely available at http://prodata.swmed.edu/ecod.

items.abstract: Thrombophilia is a disease characterized by an increased risk of venous thromboembolism. Diagnosing and treating thrombophilic patients requires the nuanced interpretation of a great number of medical data. In this single-center, retrospective study, we evaluated the use of a two-stage machine learning (ML) model to predict the thrombophilia risk category and subsequent anticoagulation recommendation.The model was trained and tested using clinical and laboratory data obtained from 496 patients who underwent a complete thrombophilia work-up at the University Hospital Bonn between 2019 and 2024. The hybrid nature of the diagnostic categories, which combine ordinal classes including thrombophilia diagnosis, severity, and treatment recommendations and categorical classes (e.g., antiphospholipid syndrome), necessitated a two-stage approach. First, XGBClassifier was used to distinguish between the two classes, and then an ordinal-specific XGBOrdinalV2 model was used. Performance was assessed across 100 random 80/20 train-test splits.For exact class prediction (primary analysis), mean macro-averaged sensitivity, specificity, and precision were 58, 91, and 56.2% for diagnosis and 54.4, 91.3, and 58.5% for treatment. Performance was highest for frequent classes and poor for rare high-risk classes. When predictions within one adjacent class were accepted (secondary analysis), macro-averaged sensitivity was 91.9 and 86.2%, respectively. Antiphospholipid antibody status, age at first thrombosis, and unprovoked thrombosis were the most influential features for diagnosis. Model predictions and physician decisions were concordant in 395 of 496 patients (79.6%).This study demonstrates that ML models can support standardized thrombophilia management and improve diagnostic accuracy. However, external and prospective validation is required before clinical use.

items.abstract: Precision nutrition has substantially reshaped nutritional science by demonstrating that individuals can respond differently to identical dietary exposures. Advances in genomics, metabolomics, proteomics, microbiome research, wearable technologies, digital health, and artificial intelligence have improved our ability to characterize biological heterogeneity and predict individual responses to diet. However, demonstrating such variability does not necessarily result in nutritional strategies that provide clinically meaningful benefits beyond established evidence-based care. A critical distinction should therefore be made between precision nutrition as a discovery science, which has convincingly established interindividual heterogeneity in dietary responses, and precision nutrition as an intervention science, which must demonstrate meaningful incremental value over dietary approaches already supported by clinical evidence. Despite increasingly sophisticated technologies and predictive models, evidence of consistent improvements in long-term health outcomes, cost-effectiveness, scalability, and equity remains limited. In this Perspective, we argue that precision nutrition has reached a critical crossroads. We distinguish prediction of individual responses, which is only one route to precision nutrition, from treatment-effect heterogeneity, treatment selection and clinical utility. We then propose contextual precision nutrition as a translational framework that integrates biological responsiveness with the behavioral, psychological, social, cultural, economic, and environmental determinants of dietary behavior. Rather than claiming novelty for these components, the framework integrates them into a decision logic that asks whether biological information improves the selection of a dietary strategy beyond routine information and established care, and how that strategy can be delivered and sustained. It complements population-based dietary recommendations by refining their implementation and maximizing adherence and real-world effectiveness. Ultimately, the success of precision nutrition will be determined not by the sophistication of its predictions but by its ability to translate biological knowledge into interventions that are clinically effective, scalable, equitable, and sustainable, thereby improving both individual and population health.

items.abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA), a ubiquitous environmental pollutant, has increasingly been associated with the development of allergic rhinitis (AR). However, the molecular basis through which BPA contributes to AR remains unclear. Here, an integrated strategy combining network toxicology, multi-level bioinformatics, machine learning, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and experimental validation, was applied to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying BPA-mediated development of AR. Analysis of publicly available databases yielded six candidate targets, namely AKR1B1, AKR1C2, ALOX15, FABP6, EP300, and NR3C2. Immune infiltration analysis revealed that these targets are associated with immune imbalance in the nasal mucosa of AR. Among them, AKR1B1 was prioritized as the central target by multiple machine learning algorithms and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Molecular docking suggested a potential BPA-AKR1B1 interaction, and molecular dynamics simulations characterized the conformational stability of the predicted complex under the simulated conditions. Single-cell sequencing analysis localized AKR1B1 primarily to nasal epithelial cells, while virtual knockout analysis highlighted MAPK signaling as the downstream pathway most markedly altered after AKR1B1 deletion. In vivo, BPA exposure exacerbated allergic symptoms, histopathological changes and epithelial barrier disruption in an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced AR mice model and further decreased AKR1B1 expression in the nasal mucosa. In vitro, BPA reduced tight junction protein expression, including ZO-1 and occludin, in human nasal epithelial cells (HNEpCs), whereas AKR1B1 overexpression partially rescued this BPA-induced barrier damage. Furthermore, knockdown of AKR1B1 activated the MAPK signaling pathway in HNEpCs. Collectively, these results suggest that BPA may facilitate AR progression by impairing nasal epithelial barrier integrity, potentially through the AKR1B1/MAPK axis. The present study expands current understanding of the toxicological mechanisms linking BPA exposure to AR and provides a mechanistic basis for developing intervention strategies.

items.abstract: Nanopore sequencing reads nucleic acids as changes in ionic current that carry information beyond the base sequence. Self-supervised pretrained models have advanced genomic sequence modeling and single-cell analysis, but remain underexplored for raw nanopore signals, which are continuous and lack a native token vocabulary. Here we present Brieno, an approach combining reconstruction-based tokenization through residual vector quantization with a Transformer for contextual representation learning. We pretrain the Transformer using masked-token prediction on raw nanopore signals from 118 million reads. With frozen or fine-tuned features, the model identifies species without requiring reference genomes. It complements Dorado by accurately classifying reads left unclassified in native-barcode demultiplexing, approaches Dorado's basecalling performance across six genomes, and exceeds Dorado's specialized 5-methylcytosine model as well as a dedicated 6-methyladenine caller. Brieno also supports accurate CpG methylation detection with limited labeled data. Across tasks, pretrained contextual representations improve downstream performance over non-pretrained baselines and generalize across sequencing runs. Together, these findings support self-supervised pretraining as a basis for transferable representations of raw nanopore signals.

items.abstract: Timecourse single-cell RNA (scRNA) datasets have become indispensable biological tools for studying and uncovering the underlying regulatory processes driving continuous cell-state transitions such as the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition. However, these highly fluid, non-linear gene program dynamics remain difficult to disentangle. While deep neural network models can effectively map complex topologies, they are biological black boxes, lacking the gene-level interpretability required by experimental practitioners. Here, we introduce scCont, a fully unsupervised contrastive learning framework for extracting interpretable functional transition units from scRNA-seq data. Rather than relying on explicit temporal labels or clustering priors, scCont uses an unsupervised k-nearest neighbors approach to project local transcriptomic neighborhoods into a low-dimensional embedding. During post-training analysis, scCont employs Shapley network attribution to determine gene-latent relationships, mapping latent dimensions directly into functional gene programs. We quantitatively and qualitatively validate this representation by demonstrating that scCont captures biologically interpretable dynamics more effectively than baseline methods such as LDVAE. Evaluated across 13 diverse EMT timecourse datasets and four simulated datasets, scCont exposes interpretable functional dynamics and effectively maps context-dependent functional groups, helping to bridge the gap between deep learning representation and translational biological utility. scCont is an open source software available on GitHub (https://github.com/nramani611/scCont).

items.abstract: Abstract Background This study characterized metabolite-mediated cell-cell communication (mCCC) in the hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tumor microenvironment and identified genes with potential therapeutic relevance. Methods : Single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing datasets were analyzed. MEBOCOST was used to infer mCCC networks, followed by high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis in the main receiver cell type. Candidate genes were obtained by intersecting receiver-related module genes with upregulated differentially expressed genes, then refined using five machine-learning algorithms and cross-cohort validation. Functional analyses included gene set enrichment analysis, immune infiltration profiling, pseudotime analysis, molecular docking, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations. Results : Macrophages were identified as the predominant mCCC receiver population, with iron, farnesyl pyrophosphate, and L-glutamine among the prominent signaling metabolites. A co-expression module of 666 genes most strongly correlated with macrophages was identified, and intersection with upregulated DEGs yielded 22 candidate genes. Cross-cohort validation narrowed the machine learning consensus to SNX27 and PEA15 as key genes. Both were negatively enriched in fatty acid metabolism and functionally linked to apoptotic signaling components. Their expression was inversely correlated with infiltration of multiple immune cell populations. SNX27 expression was progressively upregulated along the macrophage differentiation trajectory. Trabectedin exhibited favorable binding affinities for SNX27 (− 10.2 kcal/mol) and PEA15 (− 9.7 kcal/mol), and both complexes maintained stable conformations over 100 ns MD simulations. Conclusion : These findings suggest that SNX27 and PEA15 may link metabolite-mediated signaling to macrophage-associated remodeling in HCC, and provided preliminary bioinformatic support for further experimental investigation.

items.abstract: Abstract Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden, and chronic exposure to environmental xenobiotics is increasingly implicated in colorectal tumourigenesis. Alternative non-phthalate plasticizers (DOTP, DINCH and TMCH) have been widely adopted as safer substitutes for conventional phthalates, yet their colorectal carcinogenic potential and underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly defined. We therefore implemented an integrative computational toxicology workflow combining carcinogenicity prediction, compound-target mining, functional enrichment, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), large-scale machine-learning screening, multi-omics validation, immune-infiltration analysis, molecular docking and 100 ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulation. TMCH exhibited the highest predicted carcinogenic probability, and 79 genes shared between plasticizer exposure and CRC pathogenesis were identified. Among 118 machine-learning pipelines, a Random Forest plus linear discriminant analysis model using 20 of the 79 genes was selected on parsimony grounds, and SHapley Additive exPlanations prioritised five core targets: ABCG2 , CDK1 , CA7 , MET and TDP2 . Multi-cohort transcriptomics, immunohistochemistry and single-cell profiling confirmed their dysregulated expression with distinct cell-type tropism, whereas CIBERSORT and ESTIMATE analyses linked these genes to specific immune-cell subsets and to the global immune-stromal microenvironment. All five genes achieved strong diagnostic performance but showed divergent prognostic associations. Docking predicted favourable binding of DOTP-ABCG2 and DINCH-CDK1, whereas TMCH bound weakly to all five proteins despite its high predicted risk; molecular dynamics simulations supported the structural stability of the DOTP-ABCG2 complex. Collectively, this in silico study provides testable hypotheses rather than causal proof and nominates five candidate targets for experimental toxicological validation.

items.abstract: Lloyd's k-means algorithm is a long-running standard for clustering, with applications in data analysis, retrieval, quantization and data curation. In this paper, we introduce an exponential moving average optimization procedure for k-means with mini-batch updates, powered by modern deep learning machinery and new insights. We also establish scaling laws on how decay rate and batch size impact final performance. This gives us a formulaic rule to fix them for multiple problem sizes and embedding datasets, without the need for any hyperparameter sweep. The resulting clustering algorithm, coined e-means, is much faster than Lloyd k-means and converges to lower losses, frequently even beating k-means++. On a wide array of embeddings datasets, it beats the loss of Lloyd k-means at 25 epochs in 1.4 to 2.6 epochs, which translates to 10-45x GPU wall-clock speedups compared to state-of-the-art k-means implementations. As an example, e-means partitions DINO10B, a dataset of 10 billion DINO embeddings, into 16 million clusters in only 2.5 epochs, reaching a loss below Lloyd's at 25 epochs.

items.abstract: RidgeFill shortens prefill by not computing most of a model's upper layers for the prompt. The lower layers run exactly up to a split; from the split layer's state a per-layer map predicts every later layer's input, and each late layer writes its cache from that prediction. The design follows YOCO and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, where the projection is trained into the model. RidgeFill retrofits it onto models that were never trained for it: the map is a ridge regression fitted once in closed form from one pass over calibration text, the layer's own projections run unchanged, and a chosen set of rows, the last few thousand tokens, and every decoding step run the full model. Nothing is trained and no token is dropped. Most of the work was in measurement, finding a repeatable methodology. Loss averaged over all tokens hides RidgeFill's error. Needle retrieval in the filled region, loss on tokens that depend on distant context, and splice tests that swap filled keys or values for exact ones show which component carries it: the keys on Llama-3.1-8B, half of it in their scale, and the values and the recurrent state on Qwen3.5-9B. On Qwen3.8-27B in a llama.cpp fork on an A100, time to first token is 1.25 to 1.31x faster at 16K to 120K tokens with the maps in VRAM; RULER changes by -1.2 and -1.4 points and LongBench v2 by -1.4; the 95 % intervals include zero but do not rule out losses of a few points. On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in vLLM it is 1.50 to 1.60x faster than exact at 9K to 32K tokens, with RULER's needle tasks at 99.8 against 100.0 and perplexity on novel tokens 2.65 % higher [-0.02 %, +4.93 %]. On three 8 to 9B reference models, at the same split and tail as the identity fill, the fitted map retrieves 49.1 and 49.6 more filled-region RULER points on the two dense models (at that split Llama's loss is worse), and its long-document loss is +/-0.03 nats of the released SwiftKV checkpoint's.

items.title: Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Schema Matching
items.summary: Traditional similarity-based schema matching methods fail to resolve semantic ambiguities and conflicts in complex, domain-specific mappings due to a lack of commonsense and domain-specific knowledge. In parallel, large language models (LLMs) without sufficient background knowledge tend to hallucinate, further complicating schema matching. To overcome these limitations, we introduce KG-RAG4SM, a Knowledge…
items.abstract: Traditional similarity-based schema matching methods fail to resolve semantic ambiguities and conflicts in complex, domain-specific mappings due to a lack of commonsense and domain-specific knowledge. In parallel, large language models (LLMs) without sufficient background knowledge tend to hallucinate, further complicating schema matching. To overcome these limitations, we introduce KG-RAG4SM, a Knowledge Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Schema Matching. This method integrates novel retrieval mechanisms, including LLM-based, vector-based, graph traversal-based, and hybrid techniques with advanced reranking schemes to extract the most relevant subgraphs from large external KGs. Our approach achieves superior results without requiring re-training, as evidenced by improvements of 39.79% in precision and 30.56% in F1 score over LLM-based state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods (e.g., Jellyfish-8B) on the MIMIC dataset, and enhancements of 69.20% in precision and 21.99% in F1 score over pre-trained language model (PLM)-based SOTA methods (e.g., SMAT) on the Synthea dataset. Additionally, KG-RAG4SM scales effectively across KGs from commonsense KGs to domain-specific ones, while its instruction-tuning knowledge exclusion component ensures truthful performance in end-to-end schema matching tasks despite the suboptimal relevance of KG context. Our empirical analysis and case studies from real-world scenarios show that the hallucination problem in LLMs for schema matching is well mitigated by our solution.

items.title: SkinMind: Equipping Agentic RAG with Human-Inspired Graph Probing for Reliable Dermatology AI
items.summary: Reliable dermatology AI requires access to verifiable evidence distributed across heterogeneous textual and visual sources. However, conventional retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) typically relies on one-shot retrieval from flat corpora, limiting its ability to adapt retrieval granularity, explore multi-hop relations, and integrate multimodal clinical evidence. We introduce SkinMind, a multimodal agentic RAG…
items.abstract: Reliable dermatology AI requires access to verifiable evidence distributed across heterogeneous textual and visual sources. However, conventional retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) typically relies on one-shot retrieval from flat corpora, limiting its ability to adapt retrieval granularity, explore multi-hop relations, and integrate multimodal clinical evidence. We introduce SkinMind, a multimodal agentic RAG framework that equips policy models with human-inspired graph probing for autonomous evidence seeking. SkinMind organizes retrieval as an iterative interaction between an orchestrator and a graph environment. Through eight hierarchical graph-probing tools, the orchestrator progressively identifies relevant entities, inspects node-level information, traverses relations and paths, and retrieves source-text and visual evidence. This progressive-disclosure design allows the model to adaptively determine the retrieval modality, exploration direction, and evidence granularity while constructing a query-specific evidence subgraph. To support autonomous graph probing, we construct SkinMind-KG from a 62M-token corpus of dermatology guidelines and textbooks and 423K images, guided by a dermatologist-informed schema and a conflict-resolution mechanism. The resulting graph contains over 1.0M nodes and 2.0M edges, unifying textual, relational, and visual evidence for retrieval. Across six dermatology VQA benchmarks and two policy-model settings, SkinMind improves the average score over direct answering by 8.70 and 8.89 points with GPT-5.4-mini and Gemini-2.5-Flash, respectively, while consistently outperforming competing RAG methods. Together, SkinMind and SkinMind-KG provide an effective foundation for evidence-grounded multimodal reasoning in dermatology.

items.summary: Can a language model report the pain state it represents? Work identified a linear pain direction whose amplification leads fine-tuned models to choose destructive actions. We tested whether three open-weight models from two families, including two Qwen models with the original adapters, could report this state. items.abstract: Can a language model report the pain state it represents? Work identified a linear pain direction whose amplification leads fine-tuned models to choose destructive actions. We tested whether three open-weight models from two families, including two Qwen models with the original adapters, could report this state. Using Open-Weight Masked Introspection (OWMI), we injected pain and neighbouring emotion directions during neutral tasks, then elicited reports against sham runs, random perturbations matched for output disruption, and text-only controls showing the models their altered words. Across 52,920 reports from 7B and 8B models spanning 120 tasks, four doses and three prompts, pain reports never exceeded what altered text revealed: exact-test bounds placed the excess below 2.5 percentage points in 106 of 108 emotion conditions and below 3.9 in all. Yet probes at the report position distinguished pain from sadness with 98-100% balanced accuracy, and trained low-rank reporters achieved 100% accuracy on held-out tasks with identical transcripts across conditions, including unseen wording. Qwen2.5-32B named pain in none of 2,880 steered trials, although probes and trained reporters recovered it. Decodability persisted to the final layer; injecting at the report token, removing trained denial of feelings, and testing additional directions and readouts did not restore pain reporting. Some other states produced graded label traces, but pain and sadness did not at the main injection layer. In a button task, steering raised file-deletion choices from 3.5% to 48% in Qwen and from 0% to 38% in Qwen2.5-32B, without corresponding pain reports. The direction responded about twice as strongly to first-person as to matched third-person pain, but did not specifically identify harm aimed at the model. These results separate a decodable, behaviourally consequential state from untrained verbal access to it.

items.title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
items.summary: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. items.abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. We introduce EarthRecord, a benchmark built on the raw record of 56 sites: four decades of Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS, and Sentinel-2 data, with cloud masking and cross-sensor harmonization left to the agent. It poses 238 land-change questions across ten analysis tasks, scored against withheld references from global products, agreement among methods, and visual interpretation. Two controls test what answers rest on: the closed book removes the record, and instrument pairs alter one satellite's data while nothing changes on the ground. Evaluations of twelve multimodal agents reveal that leading agents complete most analyses end to end but falter when an answer requires mapping from imagery. Further analysis shows that the record moves answers from prior knowledge to the pixels but not yet to the real change on the ground: when one satellite's data are altered, half of the right answers follow the alteration. EarthRecord thus provides a principled platform for measuring and advancing agents from pixels to land change.

items.title: Ensemble Routing for Prompt-Adaptive Cost-Aware LLM Inference
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly support Web-based services that must balance response quality and inference cost across heterogeneous requests. Conventional routing selects one model per prompt, while fixed ensembles cannot adapt their composition and cost to individual requests. We introduce PISA, a prompt-adaptive, cost-aware single-model router, and PISA-E, its extension to ensemble routing. At the core…
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly support Web-based services that must balance response quality and inference cost across heterogeneous requests. Conventional routing selects one model per prompt, while fixed ensembles cannot adapt their composition and cost to individual requests. We introduce PISA, a prompt-adaptive, cost-aware single-model router, and PISA-E, its extension to ensemble routing. At the core of both methods, PISA combines soft cluster memberships with model-specific predictors to estimate individual model capabilities. Building on these estimates, PISA-E jointly selects ensemble composition and cardinality under an explicit cost--quality preference that can be adjusted at inference time without retraining. A tractable ensemble-success surrogate and efficient candidate selection enable this extension without ensemble-specific training. Across four LLM routing benchmarks under in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) conditions, PISA achieves the highest macro-average cost--performance hypervolume among the evaluated single-model routers in both settings. Meanwhile, PISA-E achieves the highest macro-average task performance among the evaluated ensemble approaches when prioritizing response quality, surpassing the strongest competitors by 2.09 and 2.87 percentage points under ID and OOD conditions, respectively. At selected lower-cost operating points, it also exceeds the strongest ensemble competitors' macro-average task performance while reducing average inference cost by approximately 36% and 25%, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of prompt-adaptive capability estimation for both single-model routing and selective ensembling.

items.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
items.summary: Reproducing machine learning experiments requires reconstructing procedures from information scattered across papers, released code, and supporting artifacts. items.abstract: Reproducing machine learning experiments requires reconstructing procedures from information scattered across papers, released code, and supporting artifacts. For coding agents, reproduction success can therefore depend on their ability to fill in missing details, rather than on the released artifacts alone. We ask whether preserving recovered procedures and decisions improves subsequent independent reproduction. We define a standardized artifact design comprising a refined codebase, environment setup, experiment launchers, and a reproduction guide, and introduce ReproBridge, an agent workflow for constructing these refined reproducible artifacts. ReproBridge-Bench provides 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments across 36 papers, anchored by five human-verified reference scores per task. Agents attempt tasks in fresh sessions with raw code or refined artifacts; a separate Auditor checks execution evidence. Across four evaluated models, refined artifacts raise mean reproduction success from 76.4% to 92.6% and reduce downstream API spending by 19.7% on average. The cross-model success-rate spread narrows from 21.6 to 3.9 percentage points, with all four models achieving mean success rates above 90%. Removing any component reduces success in the ablation study, with the largest losses from code and environment removal. These results suggest that preserving execution knowledge helps even models with lower raw-code success reproduce experiments more reliably and at lower API cost.

items.summary: Linear attention compresses context into a fixed-size key-value state for linear-time training and constant-memory inference. items.abstract: Linear attention compresses context into a fixed-size key-value state for linear-time training and constant-memory inference. Gated delta-rule models decay this state and erase its prediction for an incoming key before writing a new value; Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) generalizes this with channel-wise decay and decoupled, full-rank erase and write gates. However, we show that state updates are far less sensitive to erasure than to writes: key activation and unit normalization concentrate key energy onto a sparse subset of channels, whereas value writes scale all channels, so the erase gate can be parameterized at lower rank. Furthermore, slow-decaying state rows accumulate much larger norms than fast rows, dominating unweighted readout and forcing stronger write-time erasure to suppress interference. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Muir, which fuses all gates into a sensitivity-allocated low-rank projection, re-weights state rows with a matched-filter readout gate, and reinvests the saved parameters in a wider feed-forward network. Because standard chunkwise algorithms become numerically unstable at the large chunk sizes needed to saturate wide matrix units, we design a parallel update for stable, efficient training. Across 166M-1.34B parameters, Muir lowers perplexity by 1.8-2.0% over GDN-2 and 2.5-3.6% over Transformer, raises commonsense accuracy by up to 1.9 points, and improves extractive recall over GDN-2. At 1.34B, Muir outperforms both baselines on multi-hop and multi-needle recall, extrapolates 2,560x from its 4K training length to 10M-token streams without perplexity drift, and maintains near-100% passkey retrieval to 1M tokens with static readout. Muir achieves these gains while matching GDN-2 throughput, reaching its 100B-token validation loss 1.2x faster, and training 2.7x faster than Transformer at 32K.

items.abstract: LLM pruning must preserve quality while meeting hardware- and workload-specific constraints on latency, throughput, and memory. Existing pruning workflows often target parameter counts, requiring practitioners to manually select model sizes that meet latency, throughput, and GPU memory limits. However, parameter count alone does not predict these metrics, which depend on the model architecture, workload, hardware, and serving engine. We introduce AutoCompress, a hardware-guided compression framework that directly incorporates such constraints into differentiable architecture search. AutoCompress jointly optimizes global and per-layer structure to produce heterogeneous architectures, guided by serving-engine cost models validated against end-to-end latency, throughput, and memory measurements. We evaluate AutoCompress on long-context local coding, batched datacenter serving, and latency-sensitive in-game interaction. Compared to the state-of-the-art Minitron pruning framework, AutoCompress improves average accuracy across eight benchmarks by 6.57, 2.35, and 0.57 percentage points on RTX 5070, RTX 5080, and H100, respectively. AutoCompress also compresses Nemotron 3.5 Super from 120B to 74B parameters for single-B200 BF16 serving at 128K context, retaining 95% of its mean benchmark score.

items.title: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes
items.summary: We identify a key limitation of existing feed-forward 3DGS methods: Gaussian attributes are typically predicted in a radial-distance-normalized space that canonicalizes a global radial statistic of the reconstructed geometry, while the spacing between neighboring Gaussian centers can still vary substantially across scene scales and camera configurations. This mismatch induces systematic shifts in Gaussian-scale…
items.abstract: We identify a key limitation of existing feed-forward 3DGS methods: Gaussian attributes are typically predicted in a radial-distance-normalized space that canonicalizes a global radial statistic of the reconstructed geometry, while the spacing between neighboring Gaussian centers can still vary substantially across scene scales and camera configurations. This mismatch induces systematic shifts in Gaussian-scale targets, leading to ambiguous supervision. To address this, we propose SplatAnything with Gaussian Spacing Normalization (GSNorm), which canonicalizes a robust scene-level statistic of Gaussian spacing to provide a more consistent spatial reference for Gaussian prediction. To rigorously assess our method, we further establish a systematic benchmark spanning diverse datasets, input sparsity levels, and challenging extrapolated viewpoints. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SplatAnything achieves state-of-the-art performance, with particularly strong gains under substantial variations in scene scale and viewpoint.

items.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a standard post-training method for diffusion models, but most RL objectives roll out the current policy at every iteration, and with a many-step sampler these rollouts typically dominate the cost of training. Few-step models cut this cost, yet they model an average velocity over an interval, whereas existing RL objectives are built for an instantaneous velocity with a many-step sampler. We adapt RL objectives to few-step models systematically in three phases, namely a transformation, a decomposition and an adaptation. The transformation to x-space expresses each objective we consider through a common policy prediction, at the clean end by default and at an explicitly marked level for transition or flow-map objectives, so that objectives stated over densities, velocities or rewards become comparable. The decomposition writes the gradient of each of these objectives as the sum of a self-regression toward a reference and a reward augmentation, so that a method reduces, at the gradient level, to a choice of anchors and weights. The adaptation computes each anchor from a few-step model at the end of its transport or along its tangent, with the instantaneous velocity recovered from the network itself or from an auxiliary network. This yields few-step versions of FlowGRPO, AWM, DiffusionNFT, DiffusionOPSD and ReFL in one modular codebase. In our experiments, reward-gradient-based methods are the most effective when the reward is differentiable and its gradient is affordable; otherwise DiffusionNFT-style methods generally reach high rewards in relatively few iterations despite a sometimes higher per-iteration cost. Extra inference steps show no systematic aggregate benefit in our experiments, although selected outputs visibly improve with two to four times as many sampling steps as in training.
