items.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) tools, including medical chatbots, are increasingly integrated into health care delivery. While prior research emphasizes diagnostic accuracy and usability, less is known about the psychological and contextual factors that shape patients' trust and preferences for AI versus human providers, particularly among patients who have experienced medical stigma. Purpose This study investigates when and why patients may prefer medical chatbots over human providers, focusing on the roles of prior experiences of stigma, comfort with medical AI, and the contextual tradeoff of wait time. Methodology/approach Two scenario-based experiments examined trust in a chatbot versus a human provider (N=300) and choice between a chatbot and a human provider depending on wait time (N=450). Measures included trust in the provider (perceived accuracy and bias), past experiences of medical stigma, and comfort with medical AI. Results In general, participants preferred human providers. However, participants who reported high comfort with medical AI and those with prior experiences of stigma (e.g., related to weight, mental health, or gender identity) expressed greater trust in the chatbot. Moderation analysis confirmed significant interaction effects between provider type, comfort with medical AI, and stigma history. Conclusions Preferences for AI-driven care are conditional. Chatbots may offer psychological safety and perceived impartiality for patients with stigmatized identities. Practice implications Providers are often challenged with managing high caseloads and allocating appointments. Integrating chatbots in care pathways could improve access to care and enhance trust among marginalized populations, especially for low-stakes concerns, offering cost-effective, patient-centered alternatives in selected contexts.

items.abstract: Nutrition clinicians need to recognize the importance of establishing meaningful connections with their patients and family members. In this manuscript, we discuss skills for making these connections and possibly reducing the risk of nutrition-related ethical dilemmas. American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition leaders have stressed the importance of clinician-patient connections. Insights from Jonathan Rhoads, who was a developer of parenteral nutrition, indicated that availability and affability are important traits for nutrition clinicians, not just ability. These qualities reflect a patient-centered approach grounded in compassion, empathy, and effective communication. We present two examples of teaching tools designed to develop these skills in nutrition clinicians. (1) A nutrition clinician play performed at the ASPEN Clinical Nutrition Week 2015 that used spoken words and nonverbal communication to demonstrate approaches to connecting with a patient's family members. (2) A module developed for graduate nutrition students in 2025 that uses an artificial intelligence-generated role-play simulation to provide practice engaging in conversations with patients and caregivers involving crucial issues about the use of artificially administered nutrition and hydration.

items.abstract: Background Vascular geometry may impede catheter navigation during mechanical thrombectomy. We evaluated whether cervical curvature predicts recanalization success. Methods This is a retrospective single-center cohort of 160 anterior large vessel occlusion patients treated with mechanical thrombectomy at a comprehensive stroke center (Barnes-Jewish Hospital/Washington University School of Medicine, St. Louis, MO) from May 2019 to February 2021. Cervical curvature was computed using 3-dimensional vessel centerlines derived from preprocedural computed tomography angiography. Primary outcomes were successful recanalization (final modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2b) and intracranial access time (puncture→first pass). Associations were evaluated with multivariable linear or logistic regression, adjusting for age, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale, first-line device, and access route. Random Forest and Gradient Boosting models with Gini Importance and Shapley Additive Explanation explained feature importance. Results Mean age was 67±15 years; median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale 16; mean total curvature was 9.80±2.85. Median intracranial access time was 24 minutes (interquartile range, 17-32), with no correlation to cervical curvature (ρ=0.054; adjusted β=0.20 min/unit [95% CI, -0.75, 1.15]; P =0.676). Successful recanalization occurred in 86% and varied across curvature tertiles (low 91%, mid 93%, high 75%; P =0.017). Per-unit curvature increase was associated with recanalization failure (adjusted odds ratio, 1.21 [95% CI, 1.02-1.43]; P =0.028). Receiver operating characteristic-derived curvature threshold (>11.54) identified a high-risk group (adjusted odds ratio, 5.10 [95% CI, 1.88-13.84]; P =0.001). Machine learning confirmed cervical curvature as the dominant predictor, with a Shapley Additive Explanation peak effect at 11.65. Conclusions Cervical curvature independently predicts mechanical thrombectomy recanalization failure, with a threshold effect near 11.6 units. Preprocedural curvature assessment derived from routine computed tomography angiography may improve risk stratification and inform mechanical thrombectomy strategy.

items.abstract: Background Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a severe inflammatory lung injury caused by various factors, including infection, trauma and shock. The predominant pathological alteration in its late stages is pulmonary fibrosis (PF), characterised by progressive extracellular matrix deposition, architectural destruction and functional impairment. Particularly in COVID-19-induced ARDS, PF incidence has markedly increased, making it a major sequela impacting patients' long-term quality of life. Methods This review systematically examines post-acute lung injury (ALI)/ARDS PF through three perspectives: pathogenesis, prediction and treatment. Results Mechanistically, the fibrotic process involves epithelial injury and mesenchymal transition, fibroblast activation with aberrant extracellular matrix remodelling, dysregulated inflammation with immune cell involvement and clinical management-related factors. For prediction, various biomarkers (including growth factors, matrix proteins and inflammatory markers) and imaging features (particularly high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics) demonstrate clinical value. Integrated multiparameter models incorporating artificial intelligence show promise for early identification and risk stratification of high-risk patients. Therapeutic strategies encompass anti-inflammatory approaches (e.g., corticosteroids and antioxidants), antifibrotic agents (pirfenidone and nintedanib), cell-based therapies (mesenchymal stem cells and exosomes) and emerging genetic/RNA interventions. However, specific preventive and therapeutic approaches tailored to the post-ALI/ARDS PF population remain inadequate in clinical practice. Conclusions Future research should focus on elucidating underlying mechanisms, refining early-warning systems, exploring personalised treatments and facilitating clinical translation. The ultimate goal is to transition from traditional supportive care to proactive prevention through enhanced clinical surveillance, early prediction and rational intervention, thereby preventing fibrosis progression and improving outcomes in ARDS survivors.

items.abstract: Background Preoperative total body weight loss (PreopTBWL%) is widely used before metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS), yet its long-term prognostic value remains debated. This study integrated machine learning (ML), unsupervised clustering, and linear mixed-effects modeling (LMM) to define data-driven preoperative targets and characterize multi-year postoperative weight trajectories. Methods We analyzed prospectively collected data and electronic medical records from 802 adults undergoing primary laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy, primary Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, or revision/conversion MBS within a structured, protein-focused preoperative lifestyle program. Five machine learning models were trained with nested cross-validation to predict each postoperative year. Each model used only patients with that year's outcome recorded (608 at Year 1 to 83 at Year 6). From Year 2 onward, earlier postoperative measurements for those patients were included as predictors. Priority was given to Years 1-4. Top-performing SHAP profiles guided feature selection for confirmatory longitudinal LMMs. Although the LMM framework spanned the full 6-year horizon (858 repeated measures from 420 active patients), the most robust inferences were restricted to Years 1-4 because of substantial attrition thereafter. Youden Index optimization, segmented regression, and unsupervised k-means clustering on UMAP embeddings were used to define precise PreopTBWL% targets and map distinct multi-year phenotypic subgroups. Results Machine learning models demonstrated strong predictive performance, peaking at Year 2 (Random Forest R² = 0.524 ± 0.033, AUC = 0.875 ± 0.029) and remaining robust through Year 4, with PreopTBWL% consistently ranking among the strongest prognostic features. Unsupervised clustering (k = 5) revealed that preoperative behavioral engagement separated high- from low-performing phenotypes far more powerfully than procedure type or demographics. Initial racial disparities in weight-loss trajectories narrowed progressively and were no longer statistically significant by Year 4 (p = 0.1454). Linear mixed-effects modeling confirmed a robust, independent positive association between PreopTBWL% and long-term outcomes (β = 0.447, p < 0.001). Threshold optimization identified 10.5% PreopTBWL% as the optimal clinical target; patients falling below this threshold experienced a significant long-term deficit (β = -4.608, p = 0.017) that persisted after adjustment for diabetes and operative duration. Interaction terms between the threshold and surgical procedure were non-significant (Threshold × Sleeve, p = 0.532; Threshold × Revision/Conversion, p = 0.778). Segmented regression further identified a structural dose-response breakpoint at 19.68% PreopTBWL%. Conclusions Achieving ≥ 10.5% PreopTBWL% was associated with durable multi-year PostopTBWL% after MBS, and procedure type did not modify that association in this cohort. By integrating predictive machine learning with explanatory longitudinal modeling, this work shifts preoperative evaluation from arbitrary administrative requirements toward structured, phenotype-guided risk stratification and care escalation.

items.abstract: Purpose of review Digital devices play an increasingly important role in the detection and screening of cardiac arrhythmias. Atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common arrhythmia, is associated with an increased risk of stroke, heart failure, and mortality. This review summarises the current evidence on wearable devices for screening and diagnosing atrial fibrillation. Recent findings Numerous studies have demonstrated the value of wearables for AF detection and diagnosis. In addition, artificial intelligence enhances automated rhythm analysis and signal processing, supporting the increasing clinical implementation of digital technologies in outpatient care. Single-lead ECG devices provide the strongest evidence for AF detection, with smartwatches representing one of the most extensively investigated wearable technology. Limitations include motion artefacts and predominantly semi-continuous monitoring. Future research should focus on integrating artificial intelligence to improve signal analysis and artefact reduction, and on evaluating the impact of wearable-based strategies on clinically relevant outcomes, including stroke and heart failure.

items.abstract: By hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system to catalytically degrade pathogenic proteins, proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) offers unprecedented opportunities to eliminate intractable targets, dismantle scaffolding functions, and achieve deeper, more durable therapeutic responses. This chapter provides a forward-looking examination of the field, moving beyond proof-of-concept to address the critical chemical, biological, and translational questions that will define the next decade. We dissect the evolution of degrader design, from expanding the ligand toolbox to target previously "undruggable" proteins, to engineering programmable degradation platforms with spatiotemporal and logic-gated control. A central focus is placed on the deep integration of artificial intelligence, which is reshaping rational design by predicting ternary complex dynamics and ubiquitin transfer efficiency. Crucially, we confront the translational conundrums head-on, analyzing the unique pharmacokinetic /pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) relationships, the multi-layered mechanisms of acquired resistance, and the dual nature of collateral degradation in the context of therapeutic safety. By bridging state-of-the-art medicinal chemistry with clinical pharmacology, we delineate a roadmap for harnessing this transformative modality to deliver on its promise for patients, particularly in oncology, immunology, and neurodegeneration.

items.abstract: Triamcinolone acetonide (TA) is a widely used glucocorticoid for inflammatory diseases, including arthritis. Although intra-articular TA injection provides effective symptom relief, its safety profile in real-world clinical practice remains incompletely characterized. Adverse event reports associated with intra-articular TA injection for arthritis were retrieved from the FAERS database (2004-Q1 2026) and the JADER database (2004-Q4 2025). Disproportionality analyses were performed using four signal detection algorithms, including ROR, PRR, BCPNN, and MGPS. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate signal heterogeneity and robustness. Time-to-onset patterns were assessed using Weibull analysis. Endocrine-related adverse events were further evaluated using multivariable logistic regression and machine learning classification models with SHAP-based interpretation. A total of 738 FAERS reports involving intra-articular TA were identified, covering 27 system organ classes. Multiple established and potential safety signals were detected, including adrenal insufficiency, hyperglycemia, osteonecrosis, bacterial arthritis, postmenopausal hemorrhage, and Cushing's syndrome. Additional potential safety signals included type 2 diabetes mellitus, flushing, erythema multiforme, pemphigus, and septic shock. The strongest disproportionality signals were observed for injection site calcification, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis suppression, injection site atrophy, and Cushing's syndrome. Most adverse events occurred within 30 days after exposure (84.55%), with a median onset time of 5 days (IQR: 2-14). External signal consistency assessment using 112 JADER reports identified eight signals consistent with FAERS findings. Multivariable logistic regression showed that age, sex, therapy type, and reporter type were associated with endocrine-related adverse event reporting. Machine learning models demonstrated good classification performance, with random forest achieving the highest test set AUC (0.864). SHAP analysis identified demographic and treatment-related variables as important contributors to model classification. This study provides a comprehensive real-world pharmacovigilance assessment of intra-articular TA and identifies both established and potential safety signals. Integration of conventional signal detection, regression analysis, and interpretable machine learning approaches may facilitate systematic characterization of TA-associated adverse event patterns and support future safety monitoring.

items.abstract: Background Despite rapid advances in computational pathology, including foundation-model embeddings, most approaches remain classifier-based. Breast lesion pathology is an area of unmet clinicopathological need and a compelling setting for morphology-based modeling: diagnostic categories occupy overlapping morphological spectra and reflect heterogeneous pathways of tumor development, thereby posing substantial challenges for pathological diagnosis and subsequent clinical decision-making. However, approaches to delineate morphological continua across diagnostic categories and tumor development remain understudied. Here, we leveraged morphology-based foundation-model embeddings to define a morphologic state space across breast lesion categories and dissect how these embeddings could reflect a pathobiological continuum or sequence associated with tumor development. Methods To model breast lesion categories in continuous morphology space, we established a leakage-controlled, patient-aware workflow using the frozen foundation model Prov-GigaPath and the BReAst Carcinoma Subtyping (BRACS) dataset, a pathologist-annotated hematoxylin-and-eosin (H&E) breast lesion dataset spanning normal tissue, benign proliferative lesions, atypical lesions, ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) and invasive carcinoma (IC). Using the BRACS training split, we defined a train-derived principal component analysis (PCA) morphology space. We then performed two complementary analyses: normal-rooted k-nearest-neighbor (kNN)-Dijkstra graph-distance scoring to derive a trajectory-like morphology score without imposing the full ordinal diagnostic sequence; pairwise Energy distance and squared maximum mean discrepancy with a radial-basis-function kernel (RBF-MMD²) to quantify order-free distributional separation among diagnostic categories. Validation and test data were projected into the train-defined reference space to assess reproducibility. Results Prov-GigaPath embeddings defined a train-derived morphology space with category-associated organization. Without imposing the full diagnostic sequence, normal-rooted kNN-Dijkstra graph distances recovered a trajectory-like morphology arrangement from normal/benign to malignant lesions. Order-free Energy distance and RBF-MMD² further supported graded separation among lesion categories. Validation and test datasets preserved the pathological organization. Furthermore, morphological embeddings dissected DCIS heterogeneity associated with concurrent invasive carcinoma, without requiring additional molecular information. Conclusions Leveraging morphology-based foundation-model embeddings, we defined a morphologic state space across breast lesion categories, allowing nuanced positioning of breast lesions along a pathobiological continuum associated with tumor development. Our approaches pave the way for extracting biologically and clinically relevant information from routine histopathology to guide molecular testing, individualized risk assessment, and cost-efficient clinicopathological decision-making. Highlights Overlapping morphological features challenge breast diagnostic categorization Foundation-model embeddings defined a morphologic state space Embeddings allow nuanced positioning along morphological continua across categories Embeddings dissected DCIS heterogeneity associated with concurrent invasive carcinoma Latent morphological signals in H&E slides may refine individualized risk assessment

items.abstract: Background Estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR) and HER2 status guide systemic treatment in breast cancer. Multimodal models are rarely benchmarked against key biomarker molecular baselines or evaluated for cross-cohort calibration. We assessed incremental value, dependence on label-proximal HER2 transcripts, and transport of discrimination and calibration. Methods A model combining whole-slide images, transcriptomes, age and stage was developed in TCGA-BRCA (1051 patients; ER/PR/HER2 analysis sets: 1001/998/1006) and evaluated in CPTAC-BRCA (120 patients; 118/113/95). CPTAC had been observed during earlier development and included 13 HER2-positive cases. Analyses included paired model comparisons, transcript removal, alternative loss functions and recalibration. Internal discrimination used pooled out-of-fold predictions; external discrimination used fold-mean estimates, with ensemble calibration reported separately. Internal calibration and macro-AUC uncertainty were interpreted as exploratory. Results Internal AUCs were 0.943 for ER, 0.901 for PR, and 0.860 for HER2; external AUCs were 0.952, 0.937, and 0.918, respectively. External macro-AUC was 0.936 for the multimodal model and 0.957 for logistic regression using ESR1, PGR, and ERBB2 (difference −0.021). Removal of the extended 29-transcript 17q12–q21 region changed HER2 AUC by −0.035 [−0.058 to −0.013] (95% CI) internally and by −0.042 [−0.089 to −0.007] externally relative to the base-line multimodal model. For external 15-model ensemble predictions, recalibrated HER2 expected calibration error (ECE) was 0.236, exceeding the ECE reference ceiling of 0.125, while calibration-in-the-large was −1.657 [−2.373 to −1.023] (profile-likelihood 95% CI), indicating systematic overprediction. ER and PR also showed overprediction. In paired fold-mean comparisons, HER2 ECE and Brier score favoured the three-transcript model (ESR1, PGR, and ERBB2). Conclusions A multimodal deep-learning model achieved high discrimination across cohorts but did not demonstrate clear incremental value over a par-simonious three-transcript baseline, while cross-cohort calibration remained a substantial challenge. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating incremental value, calibration, and clinical utility alongside discrimination when assessing AI-based prediction models for medical use.

items.abstract: Background: In rectal cancer (RC), tumor deposits (TDs) are clinically important as they are associated with a negative impact on prognosis and affect risk stratification as well as management plans. MRI radiomics combined with artificial intelligence (AI) has been explored for non-invasive preoperative TDs detection. However, results vary across studies; therefore, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to pool their diagnostic test accuracy (DTA). Methods: This systematic review and DTA meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Diagnostic Test Accuracy and reported in adherence to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses of Diagnostic Test Accuracy Studies (PRISMA-DTA). Databases were screened for DTA studies of MRI-based radiomics predicting TDs in adult RC patients with histopathology as reference. Results: Nine studies (2589 patients) were identified. Across included studies, the bivariate meta-analysis showed pooled sensitivity of 0.765 (95% CI 0.714 - 0.809) and specificity of 0.790 (95% CI 0.750 - 0.825), with overall AUC of 0.845 and very low heterogeneity (I2 = 7.3%). In validation datasets, diagnostic performance remained consistent (AUC 0.806), with pooled sensitivity 0.751 (95% CI 0.681 - 0.809) and specificity 0.751 (95% CI 0.681 - 0.809). For MRI modality, T2 weighted image (T2WI) showed higher sensitivity (0.745) than T2WI plus diffusion weighted image (DWI) (0.697), while T2WI+DWI had higher specificity (0.809 vs 0.737) and AUC (0.829 vs 0.796), with no significant subgroup differences (p≥0.192). Models combining radiomics with clinical/radiological variables achieved significantly higher sensitivity (0.842 vs 0.657, p<0.001) and higher AUC (0.827 vs 0.752), with comparable specificity. Conclusion: MRI-based radiomics demonstrates good accuracy for preoperative detection of tumor deposits in RC. The integration of radiomics with clinical or imaging features increases the accuracy of identification. Amongst the MRI modalities, models that utilize the combination of T2WI plus DWI are more accurate than those using T2WI or DWI only.

items.abstract: Background: Previous research has shown that clinical prediction models have likely been 'hacked' to meet arbitrary performance thresholds. However, this work only assessed abstracts, could not identify models with a perfect AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) of 1, and did not examine other performance metrics. Methods We collected data from full texts and validated a large language model to extract data from a random sample of Q1 journal articles for 2025. We examined if hacking occurred in the AUC value, sensitivity and specificity, and checked if articles correctly reported the AUC value from corresponding receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Results We identified 2,001 prediction model articles that reported 15,656 AUC values. We found a striking excess of results near perfect prediction and at multiples of five and ten for the AUC, sensitivity and specificity, indicating likely manipulated data, methods or publication bias. Around 1 in 40 AUC values were reported outside of their confidence intervals, and around 1 in 8 ROC curves did not match their reported AUC value. Conclusion We have shown that not only the AUC value, but the sensitivity and specificity are being hacked, likely to help the authors publish their paper at the cost of evidence for practice. Excess models that are not representative of their true performance may misguide clinicians, distort the literature, and make it harder to find prediction models that are useful for practice.

items.abstract: Advances in RNA sequencing have established transcriptomics as a key approach for investigating gene expression, regulation, and functional diversity across both model and non-model organisms. In the absence of high-quality reference genomes, de novo transcriptome assembly remains essential, yet its accuracy and reproducibility depend heavily on the choice and integration of computational strategies. This review provides a comprehensive and structured framework for de novo transcriptome reconstruction and functional annotation in non-model systems, integrating current best practices across quality control, assembly, redundancy reduction, and annotation workflows. We systematically compare short-read, long-read, and hybrid assembly approaches, and evaluate multi-layered annotation strategies combining homology-based, domain-based, and ontology-driven methods. We further highlight emerging developments, including long-read transcriptomics, machine learning-assisted annotation, orthology inference, and multi-omics integration, which improve transcriptome completeness and biological interpretability. Key limitations in current workflows are critically examined, including database biases, incomplete annotations, and challenges in isoform resolution, particularly in underrepresented taxa. By consolidating methodological advances with practical recommendations, this review proposes a reproducible and scalable roadmap for transcriptome analysis in non-model organisms. We also discuss future directions, including the development of inclusive reference databases, AI-driven annotation frameworks, and open, containerized infrastructures aligned with FAIR principles to support global transcriptomics research.

items.abstract: Motivation Single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) technologies enable the study of three-dimensional (3D) genome organization at individual-cell resolution. Many computational methods have been developed to infer hierarchical structures from scHi-C data. However, annotating chromatin subcompartments from sparse scHi-C data remains a challenge. The recently developed scGHOST provides a framework for single-cell subcompartment annotation, but relies on a deep learning-based architecture, a multi-step upstream pipeline involving cell embedding and matrix imputation, and cross-cell information sharing. These features complicate algorithmic interpretation and make the annotation of an individual cell dependent on information from other cells in the dataset. Hence, methods are needed that annotate subcompartments directly from an individual cell’s own contact matrix, without complex upstream processing or cross-cell information sharing. Results We developed scSTEC, a computational framework that annotates subcompartments directly from an individual scHi-C matrix without data imputation, complex upstream processing, or cross-cell data sharing. We show that the estimated inter-chromosomal matrix constructed by scGHOST is intrinsically of rank 2, revealing that the geometry relevant to clustering can be represented in two dimensions. Leveraging this low-dimensional structure, scSTEC performs direct subcompartment annotation through 2D genomic embedding and chromosome-wise consensus. Across bulk Hi-C, downsampled simulations, and real scHi-C datasets (four human cell lines, adult mouse cortex, developing mouse embryos, and developing olfactory sensory neurons), scSTEC achieves subcompartment annotations comparable to scGHOST despite operating on each cell independently, while providing greater algorithmic interpretability. Furthermore, subcompartments identified by scSTEC effectively resolve cell types, capture developmental dynamics, and show consistent associations with gene expression and epigenetic profiles. Availability scSTEC is freely available at https://github.com/Ge-lab-pku/scSTEC .

items.abstract: Abstract Background Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved outcomes in advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), but predictive biomarkers are lacking. The role of paired-like homeodomain 1 (PITX1) in ccRCC remains unclear. Methods Machine learning identified PITX1 as a key biomarker. Multi-omics analyses integrated bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics (ST), data from three randomized controlled trials (IMmotion151, CheckMate025, JAVELIN Renal 101) and West China Hospital ccRCC cohort. Results PITX1 was upregulated in ccRCC, associated with BAP1 mutation and hypomethylation. scRNA-seq and ST revealed the expression patterns of PITX1 in different cell clusters. High PITX1 expression correlated with advanced clinicopathological features, poor survival, and metabolic reprogramming towards glucose and methionine metabolism. Enrichment analysis suggested high PITX1 would lead to more malignant tumor biological behaviors. It shaped an immunosuppressive microenvironment with regulatory T cells (Tregs) infiltrated and elevated immune checkpoints. Crucially, high PITX1 indicates inferior benefits for patients receiving immunotherapy. Conclusion PITX1 is a novel biomarker linked to aggressive tumor behavior, metabolic alteration, and immune evasion, predicting poor response to immunotherapy in ccRCC.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) exhibits high molecular heterogeneity, and the lack of precise prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets severely limits the clinical management of high-risk patients. This study aimed to identify a robust multi-omics biomarker and elucidate its intrinsic oncogenic mechanisms and extrinsic immune-remodeling roles in the UCEC microenvironment. Methods We systematically integrated transcriptomic data from TCGA and GEO cohorts. WGCNA coupled with four machine learning algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, XGBoost, Boruta) were employed for feature selection. Single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics were integrated to map the cellular landscape. In silico virtual knockout, virtual overexpression, and pharmacogenomic analyses were conducted. Computational predictions were experimentally validated using Western blot, qRT-PCR, and immunohistochemistry in paired clinical specimens, and corroborated by CPTAC proteomic analysis. Results PTTG1 was identified as an independent prognostic biomarker, with significant overexpression confirmed at both mRNA and protein levels and predominant nuclear localization in tumor epithelium. Mechanistically, virtual knockout revealed PTTG1 drives malignant progression through hyperactivation of cell cycle, ribosome biogenesis, and glutathione metabolism, whereas virtual overexpression activated immune-related transcriptional networks including MHC class II antigen presentation. Integrated scRNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics demonstrated PTTG1 enrichment in malignant epithelial cells and tumor-associated macrophages. Drug sensitivity predictions identified selective vulnerability to MEK inhibitors, including selumetinib and trametinib. Conclusion PTTG1 serves as a multidimensional oncogenic driver and independent prognostic biomarker in UCEC, intrinsically fueling tumor proliferation while extrinsically orchestrating an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Bidirectional in silico perturbation revealed distinct transcriptional consequences, substantiated by multi-level experimental validation. Drug sensitivity predictions identified selective MEK inhibitor vulnerabilities, providing a rationale for PTTG1-guided prognostic stratification and targeted therapeutic strategies in high-risk UCEC.

items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in computational biology, yet their reliability in executing complex scientific workflows remains poorly characterized. Here, we benchmarked five LLM agents (DeepSeek V4 Pro, GLM 5.1, HY3 Preview, Kimi K2.6, and Minimax M2.7) on virtual gene knockout analyses using four computational frameworks across two single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets. All agents successfully completed the assigned workflows, but their quantitative outputs varied substantially: execution times spanned a 31fold range (61 − 1,920 s), while cross-model coefficients of variation reached 142.1%. Notably, four of five agents (80%) exhibited “silent methodological failures,” generating computationally valid, error-free code that produced biologically implausible results. Among the evaluated agents, GLM 5.1 showed the most balanced performance across computational efficiency and biological plausibility. These findings demonstrate that successful code execution alone does not ensure scientific validity and highlight cross-model concordance and biological validation as important quality-control strategies for Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted computational biology workflows.

items.abstract: Abstract Purpose: To develop and evaluate machine learning models integrating three-dimensional (3D) thrombus radiomic features from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) with clinical variables to differentiate large-artery atherosclerosis (LAA) from cardioembolism (CE) in patients with acute middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). Materials and Methods: This retrospective two-center study included 453 patients with acute MCAO who underwent endovascular treatment (EVT). The 3D thrombus region was segmented on preoperative CTA, and radiomic features reflecting intensity, texture, and morphology were extracted. Multiple machine learning models integrating radiomic and clinical variables were developed using the training cohort and evaluated in a held-out test cohort. Discrimination, calibration, SHAP-based interpretability, feature importance, and decision curve analysis were assessed. Results: Among the evaluated models, the random forest (RF) model showed competitive performance in the held-out test cohort, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.822, sensitivity of 0.867, and the lowest Brier score (0.171) among the evaluated models. Both clinical and 3D thrombus radiomic features contributed to model predictions. Intraprocedural tirofiban use, admission LDL-C level, sex, admission NIHSS score, and selected thrombus texture and morphological features were important predictors. Decision curve analysis indicated positive net benefit over treat-all and treat-none strategies across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.05–0.60. Conclusion: Three-dimensional thrombus radiomics from routine preoperative CTA combined with clinical variables may help differentiate LAA from CE in acute MCAO. The interpretable RF model may serve as a complementary tool for acute-phase stroke etiological assessment.

items.abstract: Abstract Segmentation is a major bottleneck in three-dimensional morphological analysis. Although artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation workflows can be used to address this issue, their implementations are constrained by dedicated software environments or local computing resources. To address these challenges, we developed SegRef3D Lite, a browser-based platform that integrates two complementary artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation approaches (namely, SegAnything and SegCT/MRI) within a common human-in-the-loop workflow. SegAnything provides general-purpose, prompt-based segmentation by using Segment Anything Model 2, and SegCT/MRI provides anatomy-specific segmentations of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging datasets by using TotalSegmentator. Both approaches generate segmentation masks that can be imported into the same browser-based workspace for visual review, manual correction, quantitative volume measurement, three-dimensional visualization, and surface-model export. In this workspace, routine image handling and refinement are performed locally in the browser, whereas artificial intelligence inference is executed through user-initiated Google Colaboratory workflows, thus eliminating the need for a compatible graphics processing unit on a local computer. We applied our platform to serial block-face photographs, volumetric computed tomography, serial light microscopy, serial electron microscopy, and human abdominal computed tomography. Across these diverse imaging modalities and spatial scales, our platform is able to process outputs from different segmentation approaches by using the same downstream workflow for review, refinement, quantitative analysis, and three-dimensional reconstruction. Therefore, SegRef3D Lite provides an accessible framework for integrating complementary artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation strategies with researcher-guided verification and quantitative morphological analysis. Mini-abstract : SegRef3D Lite integrates general-purpose and anatomy-specific artificial intelligence–assisted segmentation with browser-based human refinement, volume measurement, and three-dimensional reconstruction across diverse morphological imaging modalities.

items.abstract: Abstract Objective To develop and preliminarily evaluate a multimodal model integrating clinical data and dual-plane magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features to predict 1-year patient-reported lower-limb numbness improvement after tubular microdiscectomy (TMD). Materials and Methods This retrospective two-center study included 214 adults: 111 in the training cohort, 48 in the internal validation cohort, and 55 in the external validation cohort. Mean ages were 53.2 ± 15.0, 54.1 ± 14.1, and 51.4 ± 14.7 years, respectively; male participants comprised 58 (52.3%), 28 (58.3%), and 28 (50.9%), and female participants 53 (47.7%), 20 (41.7%), and 27 (49.1%), respectively. Deep features were extracted from sagittal and transverse T2-weighted MRI using residual networks and combined with clinical variables in a support vector machine. Outcome-informed feature selection and tuning were confined to the training cohort using 10-fold cross-validation. Candidate models and the decision threshold were selected using Hospital 1 internal validation data. ComBat parameters were estimated from Hospital 1 training data and applied to Hospital 2 without re-estimation; Hospital 2 did not inform model development. Results The final combined model incorporated 25 dual-plane MRI-derived features and four clinical variables. It yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.868 in the Hospital 1 internal validation cohort used for model selection and 0.833 (95% CI, 0.720–0.947) in the Hospital 2 external validation cohort. Comparisons with the clinical-only and dual-plane imaging-only models were descriptive and should be interpreted as exploratory. Conclusion This study provides preliminary model-development evidence that clinical and dual-plane MRI features may aid prediction of 1-year patient-reported numbness improvement after TMD. Larger prospective, multicenter, multivendor studies using validated sensory outcomes are needed before individualized clinical application.

items.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can now process hour-long videos, making extended multi-turn dialogue over a single video a natural mode of use. Sustaining such a dialogue requires more than answering each question in isolation: the model must retrieve and reuse information established earlier in the conversation, both what it has seen and what it has said, an ability we term in-context video memory. Existing video QA benchmarks leave this ability unmeasured: their questions are mutually independent, never reference one another, and each is answerable from the video alone, so nothing ever requires carrying information across turns. We introduce VideoMemBench, in which each sample pairs a single video with a long multi-turn dialogue, whose turns are connected by typed cross-turn dependencies: an Episodic Dependency refers back to a visual episode described in an earlier turn, probing memory of what the model has seen, while an Answer Dependency builds on the model's own earlier answer, probing memory of what the model has said. Every dependency is verified considering two properties: 1) necessity, meaning the question cannot be answered without its earlier turns, and 2) non-leakage, meaning the question does not restate the information from its earlier turns. To enforce these properties, we design a construction pipeline with three LLM roles: a planner, a generator, and a judger, with each dialogue reviewed by human experts. VideoMemBench comprises 326 videos with 2,476 turns, of which 1,387 depend on earlier turns, including multi-parent dependencies and long-range call-back. Among over 20 evaluated open- and closed-source MLLMs, Claude Opus 5 performs the best with an overall score of only 45.7%, highlighting the challenge of in-context video memory. Our dataset and evaluation are released.

items.abstract: A speech deepfake detector estimates whether a recording is synthetic, but a forensic analyst also asks which system produced it, whether recordings share a source, and what evidence supports each conclusion. We present VeriSpoof, an audio language model that unifies five tasks with shared weights: deepfake detection, generator attribution (generator, acoustic model and vocoder), recording-condition analysis, synthesized-span localisation, and source verification. Each decision is supported by grounded rationales whose statements can be independently verified. Answers are scored by sentence likelihood, allowing detection and source verification to be thresholded without separate heads. Rationale statements can be checked against waveform measurements, span labels, or generator metadata. Counterfactual examples train decisions to follow the stated evidence. Across the 14 Speech-DF-Arena test sets, VeriSpoof-Plus achieves 2.14% pooled EER, ranking third of 28 systems and first among open-weight systems. VeriSpoof-Base, trained only on official training splits of eight corpora, achieves 4.43% EER, less than half that of the next open-weight detector. With the same weights, VeriSpoof-Plus verifies whether recordings from generators unseen in training share a source at 6.2% EER. Controlled studies show that the audio representation governs detection, the LLM governs recording comparison, and source supervision is necessary for neural-codec fakes. Statement-checkable rationales catch partial fakes missed by one-step answers (99.6% vs. 78.4% on PartialEdit) and determine decisions under edits unseen in training (99.5%). Training updates only 29.7M of 2.85B parameters, fitting a single 24 GB GPU with gradient checkpointing. We release both models, inference code, a demo, and VeriSpoof-Bench, the evaluation suite covering these questions.
